updated_at.description: Timestamp indicating when the preference record was last modified. This field is automatically updated whenever preference settings are changed, providing visibility into preference modification history and ensuring accurate tracking of customer preference evolution over time.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp indicating when the preference record was soft deleted for data retention purposes. Supports GDPR compliance by allowing preference removal while preserving historical data for audit trails. Null values indicate active preferences that have not been deleted.

customer.description: Customer account reference providing ownership context for the preference settings. Links the preference record to the specific customer who owns and manages these settings. The summary representation includes essential customer identification information while maintaining data security by excluding sensitive customer details.

IShoppingMallUserPreference.description:
Customer preferences entity for personalization and user experience customization in the shopping mall platform.

Stores various user settings and preferences that affect how the platform behaves for individual customers, including notification preferences, display settings, privacy controls, and other personalization options that enhance the shopping experience. Each preference record represents a specific configuration choice made by a customer to tailor their interaction with the platform.

Supports GDPR compliance by allowing customers to control their data and experience preferences through comprehensive preference management capabilities. The entity maintains relationships with customer accounts for ownership tracking and provides audit trails through timestamp fields that track preference lifecycle events.

Used across multiple API operations including preference creation, retrieval, updating, and deletion. The preference system enables customers to personalize their shopping experience according to individual preferences while maintaining platform consistency and security standards.

page.description: Page number for paginated results, starting from 1. Controls which page of preference records to retrieve when browsing through large sets of customer preferences. Used in conjunction with the limit parameter to implement efficient pagination for preference management interfaces.

limit.description: Number of preference records to return per page, with a maximum limit of 100 records. Controls the size of result sets returned by preference search operations, balancing performance considerations with user experience requirements for preference management interfaces.

search.description: Search term for filtering preferences by type, key, or value content. Supports partial matching across preference_type, preference_key, and preference_value fields to help customers quickly locate specific preference settings within their preference collection.

preference_type.description: Filter by specific preference type such as notification, display, privacy, or other personalization categories. Enables customers to focus on preferences within specific functional areas when managing their preference settings across different platform features.

preference_key.description: Filter by specific preference key identifier to locate individual preference settings within preference type categories. Useful for targeting specific preference configurations when customers need to modify or review particular preference settings.

preference_value.description: Filter by preference value content to locate preferences with specific configuration values. Supports searching for preferences based on their current setting values, enabling customers to find preferences with particular configurations across their preference collection.

category.description: Filter by preference category to group related preferences together for management purposes. Categories provide organizational structure for preference management, allowing customers to work with logically grouped preference sets.

is_active.description: Filter by active status to separate currently active preferences from inactive ones. Enables customers to review only active preferences affecting their current experience or focus on inactive preferences for potential reactivation.

created_at.description: Filter by exact creation date to locate preferences created at specific times. Useful for auditing preference creation history and tracking preference management activities within specific timeframes.

created_at_start.description: Start date for filtering preferences by creation date range. Combined with created_at_end to define a time window for preference creation, enabling temporal analysis of preference management activities.

created_at_end.description: End date for filtering preferences by creation date range. Combined with created_at_start to define a time window for preference creation, supporting comprehensive preference history analysis.

updated_at_start.description: Start date for filtering preferences by modification date range. Enables customers to focus on preferences that were updated within specific time periods, useful for tracking preference evolution and recent changes.

updated_at_end.description: End date for filtering preferences by modification date range. Combined with updated_at_start to define a time window for preference modifications, supporting analysis of preference update patterns.

oneOf.description: Sort results by creation timestamp to organize preferences chronologically by when they were initially created.
Sort results by modification timestamp to organize preferences by when they were last updated.
Sort results by preference type to group similar preference categories together for efficient management.
Sort results by category to organize preferences according to their organizational grouping structure.

order_by.description: Field specification for sorting preference search results. Determines the primary sorting criterion for organizing returned preference records in the search results, enabling customers to view preferences in their preferred organizational order.

oneOf.description: Sort in ascending order to organize preferences from lowest to highest values based on the specified order_by field.
Sort in descending order to organize preferences from highest to lowest values based on the specified order_by field.

order_direction.description: Direction specification for sorting preference search results. Controls whether preferences are sorted in ascending or descending order according to the specified sorting field, providing flexibility in result organization.

IShoppingMallUserPreference.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for comprehensive customer preference filtering and management.

This DTO provides extensive search and filtering capabilities for customer preference records, enabling customers to efficiently manage their preference settings through targeted search operations. The filtering parameters support multiple search dimensions including preference type, key, value content, category grouping, activation status, and temporal ranges for both creation and modification timestamps.

The operation supports sophisticated pagination with configurable page sizes and flexible sorting options. Customers can sort their preferences by creation date, update date, preference type, or category in either ascending or descending order, providing complete control over how preference results are organized and presented.

Enhanced filtering capabilities enable complete atomic operations where clients can perform all preference searches and filtering in a single API call, eliminating the need for multiple requests and improving the efficiency of preference management workflows. The comprehensive parameter set ensures customers can precisely target the specific preference subsets they need to manage.

preference_type.description:
Type of preference being created, such as notification, display, privacy, or other personalization categories.

Defines the category of user experience customization that this preference controls. Common types include notification settings (email frequency, push notifications), display preferences (theme, language, layout), privacy controls (data sharing, visibility settings), and shopping behavior preferences (recommendation frequency, auto-save cart).

Each preference type must be unique within the customer's account when combined with the preference key, as enforced by the composite unique constraint in the Prisma schema. The system validates that preference types adhere to platform-defined categories to maintain consistency across customer experiences.

preference_key.description:
Specific identifier for the preference setting, used to uniquely identify the preference type within the customer's account.

Acts as a technical identifier that distinguishes between different preference settings within the same preference type category. For example, within 'notification' type, keys might include 'email_frequency', 'push_order_updates', or 'marketing_emails'.

The combination of preference_type and preference_key must be unique per customer account, ensuring that customers cannot create duplicate preference settings. This uniqueness constraint is enforced at the database level and validated during preference creation operations.

preference_value.description:
Value of the preference setting, containing the actual configuration or setting chosen by the customer.

Represents the customer's chosen value for the specific preference setting. Values can range from simple boolean flags ('true'/'false') to complex JSON configurations depending on the preference type and key combination.

The system validates preference values against type-specific constraints and formats to ensure data integrity. For example, notification frequency preferences might accept values like 'immediate', 'daily', 'weekly', while theme preferences might accept 'light', 'dark', or 'auto'.

category.description:
Organizational category for grouping related preferences together for better management and display.

Provides an optional organizational layer that helps customers and administrators group related preferences for easier management. Categories might include 'communication', 'appearance', 'privacy', 'shopping', or custom organizational groups defined by the customer.

This field supports hierarchical organization of preferences without requiring complex data structures. When specified, preferences can be filtered and displayed by category in user interfaces, improving the customer experience for preference management.

IShoppingMallUserPreference.ICreate.description:
Data structure for creating new customer preference settings in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO represents the essential business data required when customers establish new personalization settings for their shopping experience. It captures the core preference configuration while excluding system-managed fields that are handled automatically by the platform infrastructure.

The operation validates that the preference type and key combination is unique for the customer account, as enforced by the composite unique constraint @@unique([shopping_mall_customer_id, preference_type, preference_key]) in the Prisma schema. This ensures customers cannot create duplicate preference settings that would cause conflicts in their user experience.

Security considerations include server-side injection of customer identity from verified JWT authentication tokens, preventing customers from creating preferences for other accounts. The system automatically sets activation status to active, creation timestamps, and customer association during the creation process, ensuring data integrity and audit trail compliance.

preference_type.description:
Original preference type that cannot be modified after creation.

This field represents the immutable preference type established when the preference was originally created. The preference type defines the category of user experience customization and cannot be changed to maintain data consistency and prevent conflicts in customer preference management.

While included in the update DTO for reference purposes, attempts to modify this field will be ignored by the update operation. The system preserves the original preference type to ensure that customer preferences remain stable and predictable throughout their lifecycle.

preference_key.description:
Original preference key that cannot be modified after creation.

This field represents the immutable preference key established when the preference was originally created. The preference key serves as the technical identifier within the preference type category and cannot be changed to maintain the unique constraint relationship with the customer account.

While included in the update DTO for reference purposes, attempts to modify this field will be ignored by the update operation. The system preserves the original preference key to ensure data integrity and prevent conflicts with existing preference configurations.

preference_value.description:
Updated value of the preference setting, containing the new configuration or setting chosen by the customer.

This is the primary field that customers can modify during preference updates. It represents the customer's new chosen value for the specific preference setting, which can range from simple boolean flags to complex JSON configurations depending on the preference type.

The system validates updated preference values against type-specific constraints and formats to ensure data integrity. Validation rules ensure that the new value adheres to platform guidelines and maintains compatibility with the existing preference type and key combination.

category.description:
Updated organizational category for grouping related preferences together for better management.

Customers can modify the organizational category to better reflect how they want to group and manage their preferences. This field supports flexible reorganization of preference groupings without affecting the core preference functionality.

When updated, the system applies the new category immediately, allowing customers to refine their preference organization as their needs evolve. The category field remains optional, supporting both categorized and uncategorized preference management approaches.

is_active.description:
Updated activation status indicating whether this preference setting should be currently active.

Customers can temporarily disable preferences without deleting them by setting this field to false. This allows for preference management flexibility, enabling customers to experiment with different settings or temporarily opt-out of certain features.

The system respects the activation status when applying preferences to the customer experience. Inactive preferences are ignored during preference evaluation, providing customers with fine-grained control over their user experience customization.

IShoppingMallUserPreference.IUpdate.description:
Data structure for updating existing customer preference settings in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO supports partial updates to customer preference settings, enabling customers to modify specific aspects of their preferences without requiring complete reconfiguration. The design follows the Partial<T> pattern where all fields are optional, providing maximum flexibility for incremental preference adjustments.

Security measures include comprehensive ownership verification, ensuring that customers can only update preferences that belong to their authenticated account. The system validates that the preference exists and that the requesting customer has legitimate ownership before allowing any modifications to prevent unauthorized access.

The operation preserves immutable fields (preference_type and preference_key) by ignoring update attempts on these fields, maintaining data consistency and preventing conflicts with the composite unique constraint. The system automatically updates the modification timestamp when changes are applied, providing an audit trail for preference evolution over time.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user preference record. Generated automatically using UUID v4 format for secure and globally unique identification. Used for database operations and preference management.

preference_type.description: Category classification for organizing user preferences by functional area. Common types include notification settings, display preferences, privacy controls, communication options, and accessibility features. Helps organize preferences for better user experience management.

preference_key.description: Specific identifier for individual preference settings within a preference type. Examples include 'email_notifications', 'theme_preference', 'language_setting', or 'auto_save_interval'. Enables granular control over user experience customization.

preference_value.description: Current setting value for the user preference. Stores configuration data such as boolean flags ('true'/'false'), numeric values ('15'), or string options ('dark_mode'). Supports flexible preference storage for various configuration needs.

is_active.description: Indicates whether this preference setting is currently enabled and being applied. Inactive preferences are stored for historical purposes but do not affect user experience. Allows users to temporarily disable preferences without losing their configuration.

customer.description: Customer account associated with these preference settings. Links to the customer entity that owns and controls these preferences. Essential for maintaining proper data relationships and access control.

IShoppingMallUserPreference.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of customer preferences for efficient listing and management interfaces.

Provides essential preference information without exposing sensitive administrative details or timestamps. Optimized for performance in preference overview screens, quick management interfaces, and customer profile displays.

Includes core preference identification fields (type, key, value) and active status while excluding timestamps and categorization details for lightweight representation. The customer relationship is preserved to maintain proper data context and access control.

Used in customer preference management dashboards, administrative interfaces for customer support, and system configuration tools where quick preference reference is needed without full administrative overhead.

date_range.description: Time period specification for filtering sales data analysis. Defines start and end dates for analyzing sales performance within specific timeframes. Supports flexible reporting periods from daily snapshots to multi-year trend analysis.

group_by.description: Dimensions for aggregating and categorizing sales statistics. Multiple grouping options can be combined for multi-dimensional analysis. Common groupings include time periods (day/week/month), business entities (seller/customer), and product categories.

filters.description: Criteria for narrowing down sales data to specific segments. Includes status filters, amount ranges, seller/customer selection, and category restrictions. Enables targeted analysis of specific business segments.

metrics.description: Performance indicators to calculate and include in the statistics report. Multiple metrics can be requested simultaneously for comprehensive business intelligence. Includes financial, volume, and efficiency measurements.

pagination.description: Controls for managing large result sets through pagination. Optional parameter that enables efficient handling of extensive statistical data across multiple pages when needed.

IShoppingMallSaleStatistics.IRequest.description:
Comprehensive request structure for sales analytics and business intelligence reporting.

This schema defines the complete query framework for extracting meaningful insights from sales data across the shopping mall platform. It supports sophisticated filtering, multi-dimensional grouping, and comprehensive metric calculations for detailed performance analysis.

The request enables administrators and sellers to analyze sales performance from multiple perspectives including time-based trends, seller performance comparisons, customer purchasing patterns, and category performance metrics. Security controls ensure that users can only access data appropriate to their role - administrators see system-wide statistics while sellers view only their own performance data.

Used for business intelligence dashboards, performance reporting, strategic planning, and operational optimization. The flexible structure supports everything from high-level executive summaries to detailed operational analytics for specific business segments.

date_range.description:
Time period filter for product performance analysis across the shopping mall platform.

Specifies the date range for analyzing product statistics, allowing administrators and sellers to focus on specific time periods for performance evaluation. Supports flexible date filtering including recent performance analysis, seasonal trends, and historical comparisons.

The date range can be configured to analyze daily, weekly, monthly, or custom time periods. When no date range is specified, the system defaults to analyzing data from the last 30 days to provide recent performance insights.

oneOf.description: Group product statistics by category to analyze performance across different product classifications
Group product statistics by seller to evaluate individual merchant performance and contribution
Group product statistics by price segments to analyze performance across different pricing tiers
Group product statistics by product status to analyze lifecycle management and availability patterns
Group product statistics by inventory levels to assess stock management and turnover rates
Group product statistics by individual products for detailed item-level performance analysis

group_by.description:
Dimensions to group product statistics by for comprehensive performance analysis.

Multiple grouping dimensions can be combined to create multi-dimensional analysis views. For example, grouping by both category and seller provides insights into merchant performance within specific product classifications.

Grouping enables comparative analysis across different segments of the product catalog, helping identify performance patterns, opportunities for improvement, and strategic insights for catalog management.

filters.description:
Advanced filter criteria for targeted product data analysis.

Enables precise filtering of product statistics based on specific criteria including categories, sellers, status, pricing, inventory levels, and product conditions. Filters help focus analysis on relevant product segments and exclude irrelevant data.

Multiple filters can be combined to create complex query conditions. For example, filtering by specific categories and price ranges allows analysis of premium products within targeted merchandise categories.

oneOf.description: Calculate total sales volume metrics including units sold and transaction counts
Calculate revenue performance metrics including total sales value and average order value
Calculate inventory turnover rates and stock movement efficiency metrics
Calculate product popularity indicators including view counts, conversion rates, and customer engagement
Calculate pricing analysis metrics including price distribution, discount effectiveness, and margin analysis
Calculate comprehensive performance metrics including sales velocity, profitability, and market share indicators

metrics.description:
Performance metrics to calculate and return in the product statistics analysis.

Multiple metrics can be selected to create comprehensive performance dashboards. Each metric provides specific insights into different aspects of product performance and catalog health.

Metric selection should align with the analysis objectives. For example, revenue metrics are essential for financial analysis, while inventory turnover metrics are critical for supply chain optimization.

pagination.description:
Pagination settings for managing large result sets in product statistics queries.

Enables efficient handling of extensive product catalog data by breaking results into manageable pages. Pagination is particularly important when analyzing large product portfolios or when grouping produces numerous result segments.

The pagination settings control the number of records returned per page and facilitate navigation through comprehensive statistical analyses without overwhelming system resources or user interfaces.

IShoppingMallProductStatistics.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for retrieving comprehensive product performance statistics and analytics from the shopping mall platform.

This schema defines the complete query structure for analyzing product data across multiple dimensions including sales performance, inventory management, pricing strategies, and customer engagement patterns. The request supports sophisticated filtering, grouping, and metric calculation capabilities for business intelligence purposes.

The operation integrates with the shopping_mall_products table and leverages relationships with categories, sellers, and sales data to provide comprehensive product analytics. Security considerations ensure appropriate data access controls based on user roles, with administrators accessing system-wide statistics and sellers limited to their own product performance data.

Flexible date range filtering allows analysis of specific time periods, seasonal trends, and historical comparisons. Multiple grouping dimensions enable comparative analysis across product categories, seller performance, price segments, and inventory levels. The selected metrics provide actionable insights for catalog optimization, inventory management, and strategic merchandising decisions.

IDateRange.description:
Date range specification for filtering search results and analytics data by time periods.

Defines flexible start and end dates for filtering entities based on creation timestamps, modification dates, or transaction timestamps. Both start and end dates are optional, allowing for various time-based query scenarios including recent data analysis, historical comparisons, and specific period evaluations.

When both start and end dates are specified, the filter matches entities with dates falling within the inclusive range [start, end]. When only start is specified, matches entities with dates after or equal to start (no upper bound). When only end is specified, matches entities with dates before or equal to end (no lower bound). When neither is specified, all available data is included in the analysis.

The date range functionality supports various business use cases including monthly performance reviews, seasonal trend analysis, year-over-year comparisons, and custom period evaluations. The flexible design accommodates different reporting requirements and analytical needs across the shopping mall platform.

start.description:
Start date for the range filter in ISO 8601 format.

Optional parameter that defines the beginning of the time period for analysis. When specified, only entities with dates on or after this timestamp are included in the results.

Use cases include analyzing data from a specific launch date, evaluating performance since a marketing campaign began, or focusing on recent periods by setting a start date without an end date.

end.description:
End date for the range filter in ISO 8601 format.

Optional parameter that defines the conclusion of the time period for analysis. When specified, only entities with dates on or before this timestamp are included in the results.

Use cases include analyzing historical data up to a specific point, evaluating performance before a system change, or focusing on past periods by setting an end date without a start date.

date_range.description:
Date range specification for filtering order statistics by creation or completion time.

Defines the time window for statistical analysis, allowing administrators to focus on specific periods of interest.
Both start and end dates are optional, providing flexibility for various query scenarios.

When specified, the statistics will only include orders that fall within the defined time range.
This enables targeted analysis of seasonal trends, promotional periods, or specific business cycles.

oneOf.description: Orders that have been placed but not yet confirmed or processed
Orders that have been verified and accepted for processing
Orders currently being prepared for shipment or fulfillment
Orders that have been dispatched to customers
Orders successfully received by customers
Orders that have been fully processed and closed
Orders that were cancelled before completion
Orders for which refunds have been processed

status_filter.description:
Filter statistics by specific order status categories.

Allows administrators to analyze performance metrics for orders in particular stages of the fulfillment pipeline.
This helps identify bottlenecks, improve processing efficiency, and optimize customer experience.

Multiple statuses can be selected to compare performance across different stages of the order lifecycle.

oneOf.description: First-time customers who have placed their initial order on the platform
Customers who have made previous purchases and are repeating their business
High-value customers identified through spending patterns or loyalty program status
Standard customers with typical purchasing behavior and frequency

customer_segment.description:
Customer segmentation filter for targeted statistical analysis.

Enables administrators to analyze order patterns and performance metrics for specific customer groups.
This segmentation helps optimize marketing strategies, improve customer retention, and identify growth opportunities.

Each segment represents a distinct customer behavior pattern with unique characteristics and business value.

seller_performance.description:
Flag indicating whether to include detailed seller performance metrics in the statistics.

When enabled, the response will include individual seller statistics showing order volume,
revenue generation, fulfillment rates, and customer satisfaction metrics.

This feature enables platform administrators to monitor seller performance,
identify top performers, and provide targeted support to improve overall platform quality.

include_trends.description:
Flag indicating whether to include trend analysis data in the statistics.

When enabled, the response will include trend analysis showing order patterns over time,
growth rates, seasonal variations, and peak ordering periods.

This helps administrators identify business trends, plan for seasonal demand,
and make data-driven decisions about inventory management and marketing strategies.

oneOf.description: Group statistics by individual days for detailed daily analysis
Group statistics by weeks for weekly performance tracking
Group statistics by months for monthly business review
Group statistics by quarters for quarterly performance assessment
Group statistics by years for annual business analysis

group_by.description:
Time period grouping specification for aggregated statistical analysis.

Determines the granularity of time-based breakdowns in the statistical results.
Different grouping levels provide insights at various time scales, from daily fluctuations
to long-term annual trends.

This flexibility allows administrators to choose the appropriate time scale
for their specific analytical needs and reporting requirements.

IShoppingMallOrderStatistics.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for retrieving comprehensive order statistics and analytics across the shopping mall platform.

This schema defines the complete set of filtering and configuration options available for analyzing order data.
Administrators can customize the scope, granularity, and focus of statistical analysis to meet specific business intelligence needs.

The parameters support sophisticated querying capabilities including date range filtering,
status-based analysis, customer segmentation, seller performance tracking, and trend analysis.
This enables both high-level platform overviews and detailed performance metrics for specific business segments.

Flexible parameter design allows for targeted analysis of seasonal trends, promotional effectiveness,
customer behavior patterns, and operational performance metrics.
The schema supports both comprehensive platform-wide analysis and focused investigations
of specific business aspects through its optional filtering capabilities.

overview.description:
High-level summary of key performance indicators and platform metrics.

Provides a comprehensive snapshot of platform performance including total order volume,
revenue generation, customer engagement, and conversion efficiency.

This section gives administrators immediate insight into overall business health
and helps identify areas requiring attention or further investigation.

time_periods.description:
Detailed statistical breakdown organized by specified time periods.

Provides granular analysis of order patterns, revenue trends, and performance metrics
across the selected time grouping (daily, weekly, monthly, etc.).

This enables administrators to identify seasonal patterns, growth trends,
and performance variations over different time scales.
The breakdown supports both historical analysis and forward-looking planning.

status_breakdown.description:
Distribution analysis of orders across different status categories.

Shows the current state of orders in the fulfillment pipeline and helps identify
potential bottlenecks or inefficiencies in the order processing workflow.

This breakdown provides insights into order fulfillment efficiency,
customer satisfaction metrics, and areas for operational improvement.
Administrators can use this data to optimize processing times and reduce order abandonment.

customer_metrics.description:
Comprehensive customer behavior and segmentation analysis.

Provides detailed insights into customer acquisition, retention patterns,
and purchasing behavior across different customer segments.

This section helps administrators understand customer lifecycle value,
identify growth opportunities, and optimize marketing strategies.
The metrics support customer-centric business decisions and loyalty program optimization.

seller_performance.description:
Detailed performance metrics for individual sellers on the platform.

Only included when specifically requested in the query parameters.

Provides seller-specific statistics including order volume, revenue generation,
fulfillment rates, and customer satisfaction metrics.
This enables platform administrators to monitor seller performance,
identify top performers, and provide targeted support to improve overall platform quality.

trend_analysis.description:
Comprehensive trend analysis showing order patterns and business trends over time.

Only included when specifically requested in the query parameters.

Provides insights into growth patterns, seasonal variations, peak ordering periods,
and overall business trajectory.
This analysis supports strategic planning, inventory management,
and marketing campaign timing decisions based on historical patterns and future projections.

generated_at.description:
Precise timestamp indicating when the statistical analysis was computed.

Ensures data freshness and allows administrators to track when specific analyses were performed.
This timestamp is crucial for audit purposes, data consistency verification,
and comparing analyses performed at different times.

The ISO 8601 format provides standardized timestamp representation
compatible with various analytics tools and reporting systems.

IShoppingMallOrderStatistics.description:
Comprehensive order statistics and analytics providing deep insights into platform performance and business trends.

This schema represents the complete statistical analysis derived from the shopping mall orders database,
offering administrators a multi-dimensional view of platform operations.

The statistics encompass key performance indicators, time-based breakdowns, status distributions,
customer behavior metrics, and optional seller performance data.
This comprehensive approach enables data-driven decision-making across multiple business domains.

Real-time computation from the shopping_mall_orders table ensures data accuracy and timeliness,
supporting both operational monitoring and strategic planning.
The analytics help identify growth opportunities, optimize inventory management,
improve customer experience, and enhance overall platform efficiency.

Flexible schema design allows for conditional inclusion of advanced analytics
such as seller performance metrics and trend analysis based on query parameters.
This ensures optimal performance while providing comprehensive insights when requested.

The statistics serve as a foundation for business intelligence reporting,
performance dashboards, and strategic decision-making processes
across the shopping mall platform ecosystem.

total_orders.description:
Total count of completed orders within the specified reporting period. Includes all order statuses except cancelled or failed transactions. This metric provides the fundamental volume indicator for platform activity assessment.

Used for calculating order frequency, platform utilization rates, and overall business growth tracking. Higher order counts typically indicate successful marketing campaigns or seasonal shopping peaks.

total_revenue.description:
Aggregate monetary value generated from all successfully processed orders. Calculated as the sum of order totals after discounts and before taxes. Represents the gross revenue performance of the platform.

Critical for financial reporting, revenue trend analysis, and business valuation. This metric directly impacts profitability calculations and investor confidence in the platform's financial health.

average_order_value.description:
Mean value of individual orders calculated by dividing total revenue by total orders. Provides insights into customer spending patterns and purchasing behavior.

Higher average values indicate successful upselling strategies, premium product adoption, or effective bundling techniques. This metric helps optimize pricing strategies and product placement.

order_conversion_rate.description:
Percentage ratio of completed orders to total shopping sessions or cart creations. Measures the platform's effectiveness at converting browsing activity into actual purchases.

Critical e-commerce metric that reflects user experience quality, checkout process efficiency, and overall platform conversion optimization. Typically expressed as a decimal value between 0 and 1.

unique_customers.description:
Count of distinct customer accounts that placed orders during the reporting period. Each customer is counted only once regardless of how many orders they placed.

Provides customer base growth metrics and helps measure customer acquisition effectiveness. Combined with total orders, indicates customer loyalty and repeat purchase patterns.

revenue_per_customer.description:
Average spending per unique customer calculated by dividing total revenue by unique customers. Measures customer lifetime value potential and individual customer contribution to platform revenue.

Helps identify high-value customer segments and guides customer retention strategies. Higher values indicate successful customer relationship management and personalized marketing effectiveness.

IOrderStatisticsOverview.description:
Comprehensive overview of shopping mall order statistics providing essential key performance indicators for platform performance analysis.

This schema captures critical business metrics that give administrators and stakeholders immediate insight into platform health, including order volume, revenue generation efficiency, customer engagement levels, and conversion effectiveness. These indicators form the foundation for strategic decision-making and performance optimization.

The statistics encompass all successfully processed orders within defined time periods, excluding cancelled or failed transactions. Each metric is carefully calculated to provide accurate business intelligence for reporting, trend analysis, and comparative performance assessment across different timeframes or market segments.

Used extensively in administrative dashboards, financial reporting, investor communications, and strategic planning sessions. The data supports decisions regarding marketing budget allocation, inventory management, customer service improvements, and platform feature enhancements.

period_start.description:
Inclusive start date of the statistical reporting period in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). Defines the beginning boundary for data aggregation and metric calculation.

Must be a valid calendar date that aligns with the period_type granularity. For daily periods, represents the specific day; for weekly periods, the Monday of the week; for monthly periods, the first day of the month.

period_end.description:
Inclusive end date of the statistical reporting period in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). Marks the termination boundary for data aggregation within the specified timeframe.

Ensures consistent period definitions for comparative analysis. The period spans from period_start through period_end inclusively, covering the entire duration specified by the period_type.

oneOf.description: Daily aggregation period providing the most granular view of order patterns and daily performance fluctuations
Weekly period grouping for analyzing weekly trends, weekend vs weekday patterns, and seven-day performance cycles
Monthly aggregation for tracking monthly growth, seasonal patterns, and billing cycle performance
Quarterly periods for financial reporting, seasonal business analysis, and strategic planning cycles
Annual aggregation for year-over-year comparisons, annual growth metrics, and long-term trend analysis

period_type.description:
Temporal grouping dimension that determines the aggregation level and reporting granularity for statistical analysis.

Defines how order data is grouped and summarized for trend analysis. Different period types serve distinct analytical purposes from daily operational monitoring to annual strategic planning.

The selection impacts data granularity, with shorter periods providing more detailed insights into daily fluctuations while longer periods smooth out noise for trend identification.

order_count.description:
Total number of orders successfully processed within the specific time period. Provides the volume metric for the defined aggregation window.

Enables period-to-period comparison and trend analysis. Combined with period_type, helps identify seasonal patterns, promotional effectiveness, and business cycle fluctuations.

total_revenue.description:
Cumulative revenue generated from all orders within the period. Represents the financial performance metric for the specific timeframe.

Critical for revenue trend analysis, growth rate calculation, and period-specific financial performance assessment. Used to measure the effectiveness of time-bound marketing campaigns or seasonal promotions.

average_order_value.description:
Mean order value calculated specifically for the period by dividing period revenue by period order count. Provides period-specific spending pattern insights.

Helps identify whether order values fluctuate by time of week, season, or specific events. Higher values during certain periods may indicate successful premium product promotions or seasonal buying patterns.

IOrderStatisticsTimePeriod.description:
Detailed statistical breakdown for specific time periods enabling comprehensive trend analysis and period-to-period performance comparisons.

This schema provides the foundational structure for temporal analysis of shopping mall order data, allowing administrators to track performance across different time dimensions from daily operational metrics to annual strategic indicators.

The time period specification ensures consistent data aggregation and enables meaningful comparisons between equivalent periods (e.g., month-over-month, year-over-year). This temporal framework is essential for identifying seasonal patterns, growth trends, and the impact of time-specific events or promotions.

Used in reporting dashboards, analytics tools, and business intelligence systems to support data-driven decision making. The period-based approach facilitates performance benchmarking, goal tracking, and the identification of opportunities for improvement based on temporal performance patterns.

IOrderStatusStatistics.description:
Comprehensive statistics breakdown by order status for analytics and reporting.

Provides detailed insights into order distribution across different status categories, enabling analysis of order fulfillment efficiency, processing bottlenecks, and revenue patterns. Each status represents a distinct phase in the order lifecycle from initial placement through final completion or cancellation.

The statistics help identify operational performance metrics such as average processing times, fulfillment success rates, and revenue contribution by status category. This data supports decision-making for inventory management, customer service optimization, and revenue forecasting.

new_customers.description: Number of new customers who placed first orders

average_orders_per_customer.description: Average number of orders per customer

ICustomerOrderMetrics.description:
Comprehensive customer-related performance metrics and segmentation analysis for business intelligence.

Provides detailed insights into customer behavior patterns, acquisition effectiveness, retention performance, and segmentation value. These metrics enable data-driven decisions for marketing strategy optimization, customer engagement programs, and revenue growth initiatives.

The analysis covers key performance indicators including customer acquisition rates, loyalty patterns, and segment-specific purchasing behaviors. This information helps identify high-value customer segments, optimize resource allocation, and improve overall customer lifetime value.

oneOf.description: New customer segment representing first-time shoppers who have recently joined the platform. These customers are in their initial engagement phase and require special onboarding and retention strategies.
Returning customer segment representing shoppers who have made previous purchases and are familiar with the platform. These customers demonstrate loyalty and are valuable for repeat business.
VIP customer segment representing high-value shoppers who consistently make premium purchases. These customers receive special treatment and exclusive offers to maintain their loyalty.
Regular customer segment representing consistent shoppers who maintain steady purchasing patterns. These customers form the core customer base and require balanced engagement strategies.

segment.description:
Customer segmentation categories used for targeted marketing and performance analysis.

Segments categorize customers based on their purchasing behavior, engagement patterns, and lifetime value. This segmentation enables personalized marketing campaigns, tailored customer experiences, and strategic resource allocation.

Each segment represents a distinct customer profile with specific needs and value propositions. Segmentation helps optimize customer acquisition costs, improve retention rates, and maximize customer lifetime value across different customer groups.

order_count.description:
Total number of orders placed by customers within this specific segment.

This metric provides insights into the purchasing frequency and engagement level of each customer segment. Higher order counts indicate stronger customer loyalty and platform engagement.

Order count analysis helps identify which segments are most active and which may require additional engagement strategies to increase purchasing frequency.

total_revenue.description:
Cumulative revenue generated from all orders placed by customers in this segment.

Total revenue represents the financial contribution of each customer segment to the platform's overall performance. This metric helps prioritize segments based on their revenue-generating potential.

Revenue analysis enables strategic resource allocation and helps identify opportunities for revenue optimization across different customer groups.

average_order_value.description:
Average monetary value of orders placed by customers within this segment.

This metric indicates the typical spending level of customers in each segment and helps identify purchasing patterns. Higher average order values suggest premium purchasing behavior.

Average order value analysis supports pricing strategy optimization and helps identify opportunities to increase customer spending through targeted upselling and cross-selling initiatives.

ICustomerSegmentMetrics.description:
Comprehensive performance metrics for customer segmentation analysis in the shopping mall platform.

This schema provides detailed analytics for different customer segments, enabling targeted marketing strategies and performance optimization. Each metric offers insights into customer behavior, purchasing patterns, and revenue contribution across segmented customer groups.

The metrics support strategic decision-making by identifying high-value segments, optimizing customer acquisition costs, and improving retention rates. Segment analysis helps allocate marketing resources effectively and tailor customer experiences to maximize lifetime value.

Used in analytics dashboards, performance reporting, and strategic planning to understand customer dynamics and drive platform growth through data-informed customer engagement strategies.

seller_id.description:
Unique identifier referencing the seller account in the shopping mall platform.

This ID corresponds to the primary key of the shopping_mall_sellers table and provides a direct link to seller profile information, business details, and account management data.

The seller ID enables integration with seller management systems and supports comprehensive performance tracking across all seller-related operations and analytics.

seller_name.description:
Legal business name of the seller as registered in the shopping mall platform.

This name corresponds to the business_name field in the shopping_mall_sellers table and represents the official business identity used for customer-facing interactions and business verification.

The seller name provides context for performance metrics and supports identification of sellers in analytics reports and performance dashboards.

order_count.description:
Total number of orders successfully fulfilled by this seller.

This metric represents the seller's transaction volume and operational scale within the platform. Higher order counts indicate strong seller performance and customer demand for their products.

Order count analysis helps identify top-performing sellers and provides insights into seller reliability and operational capacity.

total_revenue.description:
Cumulative revenue generated from all orders fulfilled by this seller.

Total revenue represents the seller's financial contribution to the platform and indicates their market performance. This metric helps assess seller profitability and growth potential.

Revenue analysis supports commission calculations, performance benchmarking, and strategic partnership decisions with high-performing sellers.

average_rating.description:
Average customer rating received by this seller based on product quality and service delivery.

This metric reflects customer satisfaction and seller reputation within the platform. Higher ratings indicate superior product quality and customer service standards.

Rating analysis helps identify quality sellers, supports seller ranking systems, and provides feedback for seller performance improvement initiatives.

fulfillment_rate.description:
Percentage of orders successfully fulfilled by the seller without cancellations or delivery issues.

This metric measures seller reliability and operational efficiency. Higher fulfillment rates indicate strong seller performance and consistent order delivery capabilities.

Fulfillment rate analysis supports seller quality assessment, helps identify operational challenges, and contributes to platform-wide service level optimization.

ISellerPerformanceMetrics.description:
Comprehensive performance metrics for individual sellers in the shopping mall platform.

This schema provides detailed analytics for seller performance evaluation, enabling platform administrators to monitor seller quality, identify top performers, and provide targeted support.

The metrics cover key performance indicators including transaction volume, revenue generation, customer satisfaction, and operational reliability. This comprehensive view supports data-driven decision-making for seller management and platform optimization.

Used in seller dashboards, performance reporting, and strategic planning to maintain platform quality standards, optimize seller relationships, and drive overall marketplace growth through seller performance excellence.

IOrderTrendAnalysis.description:
Comprehensive trend analysis providing insights into order patterns and business performance over time.

This schema represents analytical data that helps identify growth patterns, seasonal variations, and business trends to support strategic planning and resource allocation. The analysis combines revenue trends with order volume patterns to provide a holistic view of business performance.

The trend analysis is typically generated from historical order data spanning multiple periods (weekly, monthly, quarterly) and includes statistical indicators that help predict future performance. It serves as a foundation for business intelligence dashboards and executive reporting.

Used primarily in analytics operations to support data-driven decision making across sales, marketing, and operations departments. The analysis helps identify opportunities for growth optimization and risk mitigation.

oneOf.description: Revenue is showing positive growth over the analyzed period. Indicates successful sales strategies, market expansion, or improved pricing.
Revenue is declining over the analyzed period. May indicate market saturation, competitive pressures, or pricing issues.
Revenue remains relatively constant with minimal fluctuations. Suggests mature market conditions or consistent performance.
Revenue shows significant fluctuations without clear direction. May indicate seasonal business or market instability.

revenue_trend.description:
Overall revenue trend direction indicating the general movement of revenue over the analyzed time period.

This metric provides a high-level view of financial performance and helps identify whether the business is growing, declining, or maintaining stability. The trend is calculated using statistical analysis of revenue data across multiple time periods.

oneOf.description: Order volume is growing, indicating higher customer demand or successful marketing efforts.
Order volume is declining, suggesting reduced customer demand or competitive challenges.
Order volume remains consistent, indicating steady customer engagement.
Order volume shows significant fluctuations, suggesting seasonal patterns or market volatility.

order_volume_trend.description:
Order volume trend direction showing the movement of order quantities over the analyzed period.

This metric complements revenue analysis by focusing on transaction volume rather than monetary value. It helps identify patterns in customer purchasing behavior and demand fluctuations.

seasonal_patterns.description:
Identified seasonal patterns and recurring trends in order data.

Includes patterns such as holiday spikes, weekend/weekday variations, monthly cycles, or seasonal product demand. Each pattern is described with its characteristics and impact on business operations.

Seasonal patterns help in inventory planning, staffing optimization, and marketing campaign timing to maximize business opportunities during peak periods.

growth_rate.description:
Percentage growth rate compared to the previous equivalent period.

Calculated as the percentage change in key metrics (revenue, order volume) compared to the same period in the previous cycle. Positive values indicate growth, negative values indicate decline.

This metric provides a quantitative measure of business performance and helps track progress against growth targets and industry benchmarks.

peak_periods.description:
Identified peak ordering periods with detailed volume analysis.

Contains information about specific timeframes when order activity reaches significantly higher levels than average. Each peak period includes start/end dates and volume multipliers.

Used for capacity planning, inventory management, and marketing strategy optimization to capitalize on high-demand periods.

analysis_period.description:
The specific time period covered by this trend analysis.

Indicates the start date of the analysis period and helps contextualize the trend data. Typically covers weekly, monthly, or quarterly timeframes depending on business reporting requirements.

confidence_level.description:
Statistical confidence level for the trend analysis results.

Represents the reliability of the identified trends, with values closer to 1 indicating higher confidence. Based on data quality, sample size, and statistical significance calculations.

IPeakPeriod.description:
Detailed analysis of identified peak ordering periods with comprehensive volume metrics.

Represents specific timeframes when order activity significantly exceeds average levels, providing insights into high-demand periods for business optimization.

Peak periods are identified through statistical analysis of historical order data and help businesses prepare for increased demand through proper inventory management, staffing adjustments, and targeted marketing campaigns.

Each peak period analysis includes timing information, volume multipliers, and contextual data that supports operational planning and strategic decision-making.

period_start.description:
Start date of the identified peak period.

Indicates when the elevated order activity begins, allowing businesses to prepare resources and inventory in advance of the peak demand period.

period_end.description:
End date of the identified peak period.

Marks the conclusion of the elevated order activity, helping businesses transition back to normal operations and analyze post-peak performance.

order_volume_factor.description:
Multiplier indicating how much higher order volume is compared to the baseline average.

For example, a factor of 2.5 indicates order volume is 2.5 times higher than the typical average during this period. This metric helps quantify the intensity of the peak period.

Used for capacity planning and resource allocation to ensure adequate support during high-demand periods.

oneOf.description:
Categorical classification of peak intensity based on volume factor and duration.

Provides a quick reference for understanding the significance of the peak period without requiring detailed numerical analysis.

- Low: Minor increase (1.5-2x average)
- Medium: Moderate increase (2-3x average)  
- High: Significant increase (3-5x average)
- Extreme: Major spike (5x+ average)

- Low: Minor increase (1.5-2x average)

recurring_pattern.description:
Indicates whether this peak period follows a recurring pattern.

True if the peak occurs regularly (e.g., annual holiday season, monthly promotions). False for one-time or irregular peaks.

Helps businesses anticipate and prepare for predictable high-demand periods through historical pattern recognition.

IShoppingMallCustomerAnalytics.description:
Comprehensive customer behavior analytics and shopping trend insights for the shopping mall platform.

This schema represents aggregated analytics data that provides deep insights into customer shopping behaviors, purchase patterns, product preferences, and engagement metrics across the platform. The analytics are computed by analyzing data from multiple tables including Customers, Orders, Carts, and Product views, with proper aggregation and anonymization to protect individual privacy while providing valuable business intelligence.

The schema supports segmentation by customer demographics, purchase frequency, average order value, and behavioral characteristics. It includes insights such as customer lifetime value, retention rates, product affinity patterns, and shopping cart abandonment trends. All data is aggregated at the platform level to ensure privacy compliance while enabling strategic decision-making.

Used primarily by platform administrators for business intelligence, marketing strategy development, and user experience optimization. The analytics help understand customer preferences, optimize product offerings, and develop targeted marketing strategies based on actual shopping behavior patterns observed across the platform.

customer_segments.description:
Detailed analytics for different customer segments based on demographics and behavior patterns.

This property contains comprehensive analysis of customer groups segmented by specific criteria such as purchase behavior, demographics, or engagement levels. Each segment analysis includes key metrics and insights specific to that customer group, enabling targeted marketing and personalized experiences.

The segmentation helps identify patterns and opportunities for different customer groups, supporting strategic decision-making for product recommendations, marketing campaigns, and platform optimization based on shared characteristics within each segment.

purchase_patterns.description:
Analysis of customer purchase behaviors including frequency, timing, and product preferences.

This property provides insights into how customers make purchasing decisions, including patterns related to purchase timing, product selection, and spending habits. The analysis helps understand customer buying cycles and preferences for inventory planning and marketing optimization.

The purchase pattern analytics are essential for anticipating demand fluctuations, optimizing campaign timing, and developing personalized product recommendations based on historical purchase behaviors observed across the platform.

engagement_metrics.description:
Customer engagement metrics including browsing patterns, cart interactions, and conversion rates.

This property tracks how customers interact with the shopping platform, including their browsing behavior, product exploration, cart management, and conversion patterns. Engagement metrics help understand customer interest levels and platform usability effectiveness.

The metrics provide insights into customer journey effectiveness, platform navigation patterns, and opportunities for improving user experience and conversion optimization through data-driven platform enhancements.

retention_analysis.description:
Customer retention and loyalty analysis including churn rates and lifetime value calculations.

This property provides comprehensive analysis of customer retention patterns, including metrics for customer loyalty, churn rates, and lifetime value calculations. Retention analysis helps understand customer loyalty and identify opportunities for improving customer relationships.

The analysis includes cohort-based retention tracking, customer lifetime value projections, and insights into factors that influence customer retention and loyalty to the platform, supporting long-term customer relationship management strategies.

product_affinity.description:
Product preference patterns and cross-selling opportunities identified through customer behavior.

This property analyzes how customers interact with products, including their preferences, browsing patterns, and purchase combinations. Product affinity analysis helps identify relationships between products and customer preferences for strategic merchandising.

The analysis supports personalized recommendations, product bundling strategies, and inventory optimization based on customer behavior patterns and product relationships observed across the platform's shopping data.

time_period.description:
The time period covered by this analytics report for contextual understanding.

This property specifies the time range during which the analytics data was collected and analyzed. The time period context is essential for interpreting trends, seasonal patterns, and comparing performance across different timeframes.

Proper time period specification ensures accurate trend analysis and enables meaningful comparisons between different reporting periods, supporting data-driven decision-making with proper temporal context.

total_customers.description:
Total number of customers analyzed in this report for scale context.

This property indicates the sample size of customers included in the analytics computation, providing context for the statistical significance and representativeness of the insights. Larger sample sizes generally indicate more reliable analytics.

The customer count helps administrators understand the scope of the analysis and assess the reliability of the insights based on the volume of underlying data used for computation.

analysis_date.description:
Timestamp when this analytics report was generated for version control.

This property records the exact date and time when the analytics computation was performed, enabling tracking of report versions and ensuring data freshness for decision-making purposes.

The timestamp helps administrators verify the recency of the insights and maintain proper audit trails for analytics reporting and business intelligence documentation.

IShoppingMallCustomerAnalytics.IRequest.description:
Analytics parameters and customer segmentation criteria for customer behavior analysis.

This schema defines the parameters used to generate customer behavior analytics reports. It allows administrators to specify segmentation criteria, time periods, and specific metrics of interest for detailed analysis of shopping patterns across the platform. The request supports flexible filtering by customer demographics, purchase history, engagement levels, and specific time ranges.

All parameters are optional to allow flexible analytics generation based on different business intelligence needs. When parameters are not specified, the system uses reasonable defaults to provide comprehensive analytics coverage. Security and privacy considerations are enforced through proper data aggregation and anonymization techniques applied during the analytics computation process.

Used by platform administrators to generate customized analytics reports tailored to specific business questions or strategic initiatives. The flexibility in parameter selection enables targeted analysis for different aspects of customer behavior and platform performance.

time_period.description:
Time period for analysis (e.g., last 30 days, last quarter, custom range).

This parameter specifies the timeframe for which analytics data should be computed. Administrators can choose from predefined periods or specify custom date ranges to focus on specific business cycles, seasonal patterns, or comparative analysis needs.

The time period selection enables focused analysis on specific business questions, trend identification across different timeframes, and performance comparison between periods for strategic decision-making.

customer_segment_criteria.description:
Criteria for segmenting customers for detailed analysis and targeted insights.

This parameter allows administrators to define specific customer segments based on demographics, behavior patterns, or other attributes. Multiple criteria can be combined to create complex segments for granular analysis of specific customer groups.

The segmentation enables targeted insights for specific customer populations, supporting personalized marketing strategies, product recommendations, and platform optimization for different customer segments.

metrics_to_include.description:
Specific analytics metrics to include in the report for focused analysis.

This parameter allows administrators to select which types of analytics metrics should be computed and included in the report. By specifying only relevant metrics, the system can optimize computation resources and provide focused insights.

The metric selection enables administrators to tailor reports to specific business questions, reducing information overload and focusing on the most relevant insights for current strategic priorities.

min_purchase_frequency.description:
Minimum number of purchases for customers to be included in analysis.

This parameter filters the customer base to include only those with at least the specified number of purchases during the analysis period. Higher thresholds focus the analysis on more active customers with established shopping patterns.

The purchase frequency filter helps isolate insights from customers with sufficient shopping history to provide meaningful behavioral patterns, supporting analysis of loyal customer segments and their specific needs.

max_purchase_frequency.description:
Maximum number of purchases for customers to be included in analysis.

This parameter sets an upper limit on purchase frequency for customers included in the analysis. It can be used to exclude extreme outliers or focus on specific customer segments with moderate shopping activity levels.

The maximum frequency filter helps normalize the analysis by excluding customers with unusually high purchase volumes that might skew overall metrics, ensuring more representative insights for the target customer population.

average_order_value_range.description:
Range of average order values to filter customers for analysis.

This parameter filters customers based on their average order value within the specified range. It enables analysis of specific customer segments based on spending patterns, from budget-conscious shoppers to high-value customers.

The order value range filter supports segmentation by customer value, enabling targeted analysis of different spending segments and their specific behavior patterns for optimized marketing and service strategies.

customer_status_filter.description:
Filter customers by account status to focus on specific lifecycle stages.

This parameter allows filtering customers based on their account status (active, suspended, pending verification). It enables analysis of behavior patterns for specific customer segments at different stages of their account lifecycle.

The status filter supports analysis of active customer behavior, identification of factors leading to account suspension, and understanding of verification process impacts on customer engagement and purchasing patterns.

ICustomerSegmentAnalytics.description:
Detailed analytics for customer segmentation within the shopping mall platform, providing insights into demographic and behavioral patterns.

This schema delivers comprehensive analytics for customer segments defined by specific criteria such as demographics, purchase behavior, engagement levels, and shopping preferences. Each segment analysis includes key performance metrics and behavioral insights specific to that customer group within the shopping mall ecosystem.

The segment analytics help identify patterns and opportunities for targeted marketing campaigns, personalized shopping experiences, product recommendations, and loyalty program optimization based on shared characteristics within each segment. These insights are crucial for improving customer retention, increasing average order values, and enhancing overall shopping mall performance.

Used primarily in analytics dashboards and reporting systems to provide administrators and marketing teams with actionable intelligence for strategic decision-making and customer experience optimization.

segment_name.description:
Unique name or identifier for this customer segment within the shopping mall analytics system. Used for reporting, dashboard display, and segment management purposes.

Examples include 'High-Value Shoppers', 'Frequent Visitors', 'Seasonal Customers', or 'New Customer Cohort'. Segment names should be descriptive and meaningful for business stakeholders.

segment_criteria.description:
Collection of criteria used to define this customer segment, including demographic attributes, behavioral patterns, and shopping preferences.

Each criterion specifies the segmentation logic, comparison operators, and target values that collectively define the customer segment boundaries. Multiple criteria can be combined using AND/OR logic for complex segmentation.

customer_count.description:
Total number of customers currently belonging to this segment within the shopping mall platform.

This metric provides the segment size and helps assess the business impact and scalability of segment-specific strategies. Minimum value is 0, representing segments with no current customers.

average_order_value.description:
Average monetary value of orders placed by customers in this segment, calculated over the analysis period.

This key performance indicator helps assess the spending power and economic value of the segment. Used for pricing strategy optimization and revenue forecasting. Values must be non-negative.

purchase_frequency.description:
Average number of purchases per customer in this segment during the analysis period.

Measures shopping engagement and loyalty patterns. Higher frequencies indicate more active and engaged customers. Used for inventory planning and customer retention strategies.

retention_rate.description:
Customer retention rate expressed as a percentage, measuring how many customers from this segment continue shopping over time.

Calculated as the percentage of customers who remain active compared to the initial cohort. Critical for assessing segment loyalty and long-term value. Valid range is 0-100%.

preferred_categories.description:
Top product categories most frequently purchased by customers in this segment, ranked by purchase frequency or revenue.

Provides insights into segment-specific shopping preferences for category management, merchandising strategies, and personalized recommendations. Category names should match the shopping mall's product catalog.

engagement_score.description:
Overall engagement score for this segment, combining various engagement metrics into a single composite score.

Factors include website/app usage frequency, product reviews, wishlist activity, and social interactions. Scores range from 0-10, with higher scores indicating more engaged segments.

IPurchasePatternAnalytics.description:
Comprehensive analysis of customer purchase behaviors within the shopping mall platform, including frequency, timing, product preferences, and spending patterns.

This schema provides deep insights into how customers make purchasing decisions, analyzing patterns related to purchase timing, product selection, basket composition, and seasonal variations. The analysis helps understand customer buying cycles, preferences, and behavioral trends specific to the shopping mall environment.

The purchase pattern analytics are essential for inventory planning, marketing campaign timing, personalized product recommendations, and operational optimization. These insights enable data-driven decisions for improving customer experience, increasing conversion rates, and maximizing revenue opportunities.

Used by analytics teams, marketing departments, and inventory managers to optimize business strategies based on empirical customer behavior data collected from the shopping mall platform.

average_purchase_frequency.description:
Average number of purchases per customer over the specified analysis period, measured across the entire shopping mall customer base or specific segments.

This metric indicates overall customer engagement and shopping activity levels. Higher frequencies suggest more frequent visitors and potential loyalty program candidates. Values must be non-negative.

purchase_timing_patterns.description:
Detailed analysis of purchase timing behaviors, including patterns related to time of day, day of week, and seasonal variations.

Helps optimize store operations, staffing levels, and promotional campaign timing based on when customers are most likely to make purchases. Each pattern includes statistical significance and business impact assessment.

seasonal_trends.description:
Analysis of seasonal purchasing patterns and trends, identifying how customer behavior changes throughout the year.

Includes holiday shopping patterns, seasonal product preferences, and weather-related purchasing behaviors. Essential for inventory planning, seasonal marketing campaigns, and revenue forecasting.

basket_size_analysis.description:
Comprehensive analysis of shopping basket sizes, composition, and value distribution across different customer segments and product categories.

Provides insights into typical purchase quantities, product combinations, and spending patterns. Used for inventory optimization, product bundling strategies, and cross-selling opportunities.

cross_selling_opportunities.description:
Identified opportunities for cross-selling products based on analysis of customer purchase patterns and product affinity relationships.

Each opportunity includes recommended product combinations, confidence scores, and expected business impact. Used for personalized recommendations and strategic product placement.

IEngagementMetrics.description:
Comprehensive customer engagement metrics tracking platform interaction patterns and conversion behaviors.

This schema captures detailed analytics on how customers engage with the shopping platform, including browsing duration, page navigation patterns, cart management behaviors, and purchase conversion rates. Engagement metrics provide crucial insights into customer interest levels, platform usability effectiveness, and opportunities for optimizing the user experience journey.

The metrics analyze customer journey effectiveness from initial product discovery through final purchase conversion, helping identify friction points and optimization opportunities. Platform navigation patterns reveal how customers explore product categories and interact with search and filtering features.

Used primarily in analytics reporting and dashboard displays to monitor platform performance and customer engagement trends over time. These metrics help inform UX improvements, feature prioritization, and conversion rate optimization strategies.

average_session_duration.description:
Average duration of customer sessions measured in minutes. Higher values indicate stronger engagement and platform stickiness. This metric helps identify content quality and user experience effectiveness.

Sessions are tracked from initial platform access until user inactivity timeout. Values typically range from 2-15 minutes depending on platform complexity and customer engagement levels.

pages_per_session.description:
