Average number of distinct pages viewed during customer sessions. Higher values indicate effective content discovery and navigation patterns.

This metric reflects how well customers explore the platform and discover relevant products. Values help optimize information architecture and navigation flow design.

cart_abandonment_rate.description:
Percentage of shopping carts created that are abandoned before completing purchase. Lower values indicate better conversion funnel effectiveness.

Cart abandonment analysis helps identify friction points in the checkout process, pricing concerns, or shipping issues that prevent final conversion.

product_view_to_purchase_rate.description:
Conversion rate measuring the percentage of product views that result in purchases. This metric evaluates product presentation effectiveness and customer decision-making patterns.

Higher conversion rates indicate compelling product information, effective pricing strategies, and smooth purchase pathways. Values help optimize product pages and recommendation algorithms.

return_visitor_rate.description:
Percentage of customers who return to the platform after their initial visit. This metric measures platform stickiness and customer loyalty development.

Higher return rates indicate successful customer retention strategies, valuable content, and positive user experiences that encourage repeat engagement.

mobile_vs_desktop_usage.description:
Detailed breakdown of platform access patterns across different device types. This analysis helps optimize user experience for specific device categories and prioritize development efforts.

Understanding device preferences enables targeted optimization for mobile responsiveness, desktop feature richness, and tablet interface compatibility.

IRetentionAnalysis.description:
Comprehensive customer retention and loyalty analytics including churn patterns, lifetime value calculations, and cohort-based performance tracking.

This schema provides detailed analysis of customer retention behaviors, loyalty development patterns, and factors influencing long-term customer relationships with the platform. Retention metrics help identify opportunities for improving customer satisfaction and reducing churn rates.

The analysis includes cohort-based tracking that segments customers by acquisition timeframe, enabling comparison of retention patterns across different customer groups. Lifetime value calculations project the long-term revenue potential of customer relationships.

Used primarily in customer relationship management dashboards and strategic planning to optimize retention strategies, loyalty program effectiveness, and customer lifetime value maximization. These insights help inform targeted retention campaigns and personalized engagement strategies.

overall_retention_rate.description:
Overall customer retention rate calculated across all customer segments and time periods. This high-level metric provides a snapshot of platform retention effectiveness.

Higher retention rates indicate successful customer satisfaction, effective service delivery, and positive platform experiences that encourage continued engagement.

cohort_retention_rates.description:
Detailed retention analysis segmented by customer acquisition cohorts. Cohort analysis reveals how retention patterns evolve over time and across different customer groups.

This segmentation helps identify which acquisition channels and time periods produce the most loyal customers, enabling optimization of marketing strategies and customer onboarding processes.

average_customer_lifetime_value.description:
Average projected lifetime value of customers based on historical spending patterns and retention rates. This metric quantifies the long-term revenue potential of customer relationships.

Higher lifetime values justify greater investment in customer acquisition and retention efforts, as they represent significant long-term revenue opportunities.

churn_rate_analysis.description:
Comprehensive analysis of customer churn patterns, including rates, contributing factors, and predictive indicators. Churn analysis helps identify at-risk customers and develop proactive retention strategies.

Understanding churn drivers enables targeted interventions to prevent customer departure and improve overall retention performance.

loyalty_program_effectiveness.description:
Effectiveness measurement of loyalty programs in improving customer retention rates. This metric evaluates the return on investment for loyalty initiatives and program enhancements.

Higher effectiveness scores indicate successful program design that meaningfully influences customer behavior and strengthens long-term relationships.

IProductAffinityAnalysis.description:
Product preference patterns and cross-selling opportunities identified through customer behavior.

This schema analyzes how customers interact with products, including their preferences, browsing patterns, and purchase combinations. Product affinity analysis helps identify relationships between products and customer preferences.

The analysis supports personalized recommendations, product bundling strategies, and inventory optimization based on customer behavior patterns and product relationships.

Used for analytics dashboards, marketing campaign planning, and product recommendation engines. Provides insights into customer purchasing behavior and product relationship patterns across different customer segments and time periods.

analysisId.description: Unique identifier for this specific affinity analysis instance. Generated automatically when the analysis is created and used for tracking and referencing specific analysis runs.

period.description: Time period covered by this affinity analysis. Defines the date range for which customer behavior data was analyzed to generate these insights.

customerSegment.description: Specific customer segment targeted by this analysis. Can be based on demographics, purchasing behavior, or other segmentation criteria relevant to the shopping mall platform.

topProductCategories.description: Most popular product categories based on customer preferences within the analyzed period. Categories are ranked by customer engagement metrics including views, cart additions, and purchases.

productBundleOpportunities.description: Identified opportunities for product bundling based on purchase patterns. Bundles are suggested when products are frequently purchased together by the same customers.

crossSellRecommendations.description: Recommended cross-selling opportunities between products. These recommendations identify products that customers who bought item A are likely to also purchase item B.

affinityScores.description: Affinity scores between different product categories and items. Scores range from 0 to 1, with higher values indicating stronger relationships between products based on customer behavior patterns.

ITimePeriod.description:
Time period specification for analytics reporting and data filtering.

This schema defines the time range for analytics reports, supporting various period types including fixed ranges, relative periods, and custom date ranges. The time period specification ensures consistent time-based analysis across different reports.

The schema supports both predefined periods (like last 30 days, last quarter) and custom date ranges for flexible analytics generation based on specific business needs.

Validation rules ensure that custom periods have valid date ranges and that start dates precede end dates. Predefined periods automatically calculate the appropriate date ranges based on the current date.

oneOf.description: Custom date range defined by explicit start and end dates. Use this for specific date ranges that don't fit predefined periods.
Last 7 days including today. Automatically calculates dates from current date minus 6 days to current date.
Last 30 days including today. Automatically calculates dates from current date minus 29 days to current date.
Last complete calendar quarter. For example, if current month is April, last quarter would be January-March.
Last complete calendar year. For example, if current year is 2025, last year would be 2024.

periodType.description: Type of time period for analysis. Determines how the date range is calculated and whether custom dates are required.

startDate.description: Start date for custom period analysis. Required when periodType is 'custom'. Must be a valid date in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).

endDate.description: End date for custom period analysis. Required when periodType is 'custom'. Must be a valid date in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD) and must be equal to or after the start date.

ISegmentationCriterion.description:
Customer segmentation criterion defining rules for grouping customers based on specific attributes and behaviors.

This schema represents a single segmentation rule used in customer analytics and marketing campaigns. Each criterion specifies which customer attribute to evaluate, what comparison operator to apply, and the target value or range for segmentation.

Segmentation criteria enable sophisticated customer grouping for targeted marketing, personalized experiences, and behavioral analysis. Multiple criteria can be combined using AND/OR logic to create complex customer segments that reflect real-world purchasing patterns and preferences.

Common use cases include segmenting customers by demographic attributes (age, location), purchasing behavior (frequency, average spend), loyalty status, product preferences, and engagement levels. The system validates that operators are compatible with attribute types (e.g., numeric operators for quantitative attributes).

oneOf.description: Customer age range segmentation for demographic targeting. Supports ranges like '18-24', '25-34', '35-44', etc. Used for age-specific marketing campaigns and product recommendations.

Purchase frequency segmentation based on how often customers buy. Categories include 'infrequent' (<1/month), 'regular' (1-3/month), 'frequent' (>3/month). Helps identify loyal customers and re-engagement opportunities.
Average spending per order segmentation. Ranges like '$0-50', '$51-100', '$101-200', '$200+'. Identifies high-value customers and spending patterns for revenue optimization.
Customer account status segmentation including 'new', 'active', 'inactive', 'churned'. Critical for retention campaigns and lifecycle marketing strategies.
Preferred product category segmentation based on purchase history. Identifies customer interests for cross-selling and category-specific promotions.

attribute.description: Customer attribute used for segmentation. Determines which customer characteristic will be evaluated for grouping purposes.

oneOf.description: Exact match operator for categorical attributes. Used when the attribute value must exactly match the specified target value. Suitable for status fields, category preferences, and discrete values.
Greater than operator for numeric comparisons. Used for quantitative attributes like age, purchase frequency, order value where values must exceed the threshold.
Less than operator for numeric comparisons. Used for quantitative attributes where values must be below the specified threshold, such as identifying low-spending customers.

Range-based operator for numeric attributes falling within a specified range. Requires the value_range property to define minimum and maximum bounds. Ideal for age ranges, spending brackets, and frequency bands.
Membership operator for checking if attribute value exists within a set of specified values. Useful for multi-value categories, status lists, and preference groups.

operator.description: Comparison operator defining how the attribute value will be evaluated against the target criteria.

value.description:
Target value for segmentation comparison. The specific value that customer attributes will be evaluated against using the defined operator.

For numeric operators (greater_than, less_than), the value should be a numeric string. For categorical operators (equals, in), the value should match valid category values. For the 'between' operator, this field may be ignored in favor of the value_range property.

value_range.description:
Numeric range specification used exclusively with the 'between' operator. Defines the inclusive minimum and maximum values for range-based segmentation.

Required when operator is 'between', optional for all other operators. The range defines the boundaries within which customer attribute values must fall to satisfy the segmentation criterion.

IValueRange.description:
Flexible numeric range specification for filtering, segmentation, and analysis across various quantitative metrics in the shopping platform.

This schema defines inclusive numeric boundaries used throughout the system for customer segmentation, product filtering, price range specifications, and analytical reporting. Value ranges provide a standardized way to express quantitative constraints and boundaries.

The range supports both consumer-facing applications (like price filters in product search) and internal analytics (like customer segmentation by purchase value). The inclusive boundary design ensures clear mathematical interpretation and consistent application across different use cases.

Value ranges are fundamental to many platform features including dynamic pricing, inventory management, customer loyalty programs, and personalized recommendations based on spending patterns and purchase frequencies.

min_value.description:
Minimum boundary value for the range, inclusive. This value represents the lower limit of acceptable values within the specified range.

For price ranges, this would be the minimum acceptable price. For customer segmentation, this might represent the minimum purchase frequency or spending threshold required for inclusion in a segment.

The minimum value must be less than or equal to the maximum value to form a valid range. Zero or negative values are allowed where appropriate for the specific use case.

max_value.description:
Maximum boundary value for the range, inclusive. This value represents the upper limit of acceptable values within the specified range.

For inventory management, this might represent maximum stock levels. For customer analytics, this could be the upper spending limit for a particular customer segment.

The maximum value must be greater than or equal to the minimum value to form a valid range. Special values like Infinity may be used to represent unbounded upper limits in certain analytical contexts.

IPurchaseTimingPattern.description:
Pattern analysis of purchase timing behaviors and trends in the shopping mall platform.

This schema analyzes when customers make purchases, identifying patterns related to time of day, day of week, and seasonal variations. Timing pattern analysis helps optimize marketing campaigns, inventory management, and customer engagement strategies.

The patterns provide insights into customer shopping habits and preferences related to purchase timing, enabling better resource allocation and targeted promotional activities. This data is crucial for understanding peak shopping hours, seasonal demand fluctuations, and customer behavior patterns across different time periods.

Used primarily in analytics dashboards and reporting systems to help sellers and administrators optimize their business strategies based on customer purchasing patterns.

oneOf.description: Morning time period when purchases typically occur (6 AM - 12 PM). This pattern helps identify early shopping behaviors and breakfast-related purchasing trends.
Afternoon time period when purchases typically occur (12 PM - 6 PM). This pattern helps identify lunchtime shopping behaviors and afternoon purchasing trends.
Evening time period when purchases typically occur (6 PM - 9 PM). This pattern helps identify after-work shopping behaviors and dinner-related purchasing trends.
Night time period when purchases typically occur (9 PM - 6 AM). This pattern helps identify late-night shopping behaviors and overnight purchasing trends.

time_period.description: Time of day categorization for purchase pattern analysis. Helps identify peak shopping hours and customer behavior patterns throughout the day.

oneOf.description: Weekday purchases (Monday through Friday). This pattern helps identify business-day shopping behaviors and work-related purchasing trends.
Weekend purchases (Saturday and Sunday). This pattern helps identify leisure shopping behaviors and weekend purchasing trends.

day_type.description: Day type categorization distinguishing between weekday and weekend purchasing patterns. Helps understand how customer behavior differs between workdays and leisure days.

purchase_count.description: Total number of purchases recorded within this specific timing pattern. This count provides quantitative data for analyzing purchase frequency and volume across different time periods.

percentage_of_total.description: Percentage representation of this timing pattern relative to total purchases. Calculated as (purchase_count / total_purchases) * 100, providing proportional insight into pattern significance.

ISeasonalTrend.description:
Seasonal purchasing patterns and trends analysis for the shopping mall platform.

This schema identifies seasonal variations in customer purchasing behavior, including monthly patterns, holiday trends, and seasonal product preferences. Seasonal trend analysis helps with inventory planning, seasonal marketing strategies, and business forecasting.

The trends provide insights into how customer behavior changes throughout the year, enabling better anticipation of demand fluctuations and seasonal opportunities. This analysis is essential for optimizing product assortments, promotional campaigns, and resource allocation based on seasonal patterns.

Used in advanced analytics systems to help sellers and administrators understand cyclical purchasing behaviors and plan for seasonal variations in customer demand.

oneOf.description: Spring season (March-May) purchasing patterns. This trend helps identify seasonal product preferences and shopping behaviors during the spring renewal period.
Summer season (June-August) purchasing patterns. This trend helps identify vacation-related purchasing behaviors and summer product preferences.
Fall season (September-November) purchasing patterns. This trend helps identify back-to-school shopping behaviors and autumn product preferences.
Winter season (December-February) purchasing patterns. This trend helps identify holiday shopping behaviors and winter product preferences.
Holiday period purchasing patterns. This trend helps identify special occasion shopping behaviors and holiday-specific product preferences.

season.description: Seasonal categorization for trend analysis. Helps identify cyclical purchasing patterns and seasonal variations in customer behavior.

oneOf.description: Purchasing trend is showing growth or upward movement. Indicates rising demand or popularity for products during this seasonal period.
Purchasing trend is showing decline or downward movement. Indicates decreasing demand or popularity for products during this seasonal period.
Purchasing trend is showing consistent or stable patterns. Indicates steady demand without significant seasonal fluctuations.

trend_direction.description: Direction of the seasonal purchasing trend. Provides insight into whether customer demand is growing, declining, or remaining stable during specific seasonal periods.

impact_factor.description: Quantitative measure of the seasonal trend's strength and impact on overall purchasing behavior. Values range from 0 (no impact) to 1 (maximum impact), indicating the significance of seasonal variations.

affected_categories.description: List of product categories most significantly affected by this seasonal trend. Helps identify which types of products experience the strongest seasonal variations in customer demand.

IBasketSizeAnalysis.description:
Comprehensive analysis of shopping basket sizes and composition patterns across customer segments.

This schema provides detailed analytics on customer shopping behavior, including average item counts, product combinations, and basket value distributions. Basket analysis helps retailers understand purchasing patterns, optimize inventory management, and develop targeted marketing strategies.

The analysis supports inventory planning by identifying typical product quantities purchased together, enabling better stock management. Product placement strategies benefit from understanding which items are frequently purchased together, allowing for strategic store layout optimization. Personalized recommendations are generated based on typical basket compositions and customer segment behaviors.

Each analysis includes temporal context with timestamps and customer segmentation data, allowing for trend analysis over time and across different customer demographics. The analysis period specifies the timeframe covered by the data, ensuring accurate trend interpretation and seasonal pattern identification.

timestamp.description: Timestamp when this basket analysis was generated. Used for tracking analysis freshness and enabling trend comparisons over time. Analysis timestamps ensure data currency and support seasonal pattern identification.

customer_segment.description: Customer segment or demographic group for this analysis. Segments may include new customers, loyal customers, high-value customers, or demographic-based groups. Segmentation enables targeted marketing and personalized shopping experiences.

analysis_period.description: Time period covered by this analysis (e.g., 'last_30_days', 'Q1_2024', 'seasonal'). Specifies the timeframe for data collection, ensuring accurate trend interpretation and seasonal pattern identification.

average_items_per_basket.description: Average number of items per shopping basket across the analyzed period. This metric helps understand typical purchase sizes and supports inventory planning. Whole numbers represent actual item counts purchased by customers.

average_basket_value.description: Average monetary value of shopping baskets in the local currency. This metric indicates customer spending patterns and helps with pricing strategy and revenue forecasting. Values represent actual transaction amounts before taxes and discounts.

common_product_combinations.description: Frequently purchased product combinations identified through market basket analysis. These combinations reveal product affinities and support bundle recommendations, cross-selling strategies, and optimized product placement.

basket_size_distribution.description: Distribution of basket sizes across different value and item count categories. This distribution analysis helps understand customer purchasing behavior patterns and supports segmentation strategies for targeted marketing.

ICrossSellingOpportunity.description:
Identified opportunity for cross-selling products based on comprehensive customer behavior pattern analysis.

This schema represents specific cross-selling opportunities discovered through advanced analytics of customer purchase patterns, product relationships, and market basket analysis. Cross-selling opportunities help increase average order value, improve customer satisfaction, and optimize product placement strategies.

Each opportunity includes detailed context about the source product category, recommended cross-sell categories, statistical confidence metrics, and expected business impact. Implementation status tracking allows for monitoring opportunity execution and measuring actual performance against predictions.

The analysis considers customer segmentation to ensure recommendations are tailored to specific customer groups, increasing relevance and conversion rates. Timestamp tracking enables opportunity lifecycle management and performance trend analysis over time.

Successful cross-selling implementations typically show 15-30% increases in average order value and improved customer retention through more relevant product recommendations and enhanced shopping experiences.

timestamp.description: Timestamp when this cross-selling opportunity was identified. Used for tracking opportunity freshness, monitoring implementation timelines, and analyzing performance trends over time.

customer_segment.description: Target customer segment for this cross-selling opportunity. Segments may include demographic groups, purchase behavior patterns, or loyalty status. Targeted segmentation increases recommendation relevance and conversion rates.

source_product_category.description: Product category that triggers the cross-selling opportunity. This is the primary product category where customers typically start their shopping journey, serving as the foundation for relevant cross-sell recommendations.

recommended_categories.description: Recommended product categories for cross-selling based on purchase pattern analysis. These categories show strong affinity with the source category and represent logical extensions of the customer's shopping journey.

confidence_score.description: Statistical confidence level for this cross-selling opportunity, represented as a decimal between 0 and 1. Higher scores indicate stronger product relationships and higher predicted conversion rates. Scores above 0.7 typically represent strong opportunities.

expected_value_increase.description: Expected increase in average order value if this cross-selling opportunity is successfully implemented. Value represents the projected monetary impact in local currency, based on historical data and pattern analysis.

implementation_status.description: Current implementation status of this cross-selling opportunity. Status values include: identified, planned, testing, implemented, measured, optimized. Tracking implementation progress ensures opportunity execution and performance measurement.

IDeviceUsage.description:
Breakdown of platform usage by device type and platform.

This schema analyzes how customers access the shopping platform across different devices, including mobile, desktop, and tablet usage patterns. Device usage analysis helps optimize platform design and user experience for different devices by identifying which platforms customers prefer for different types of shopping activities.

The analysis provides insights into customer preferences for different access methods and helps prioritize development efforts for specific device types. Understanding device usage patterns is crucial for responsive design optimization, feature prioritization, and platform-specific performance improvements.

Note: The mobile_percentage, desktop_percentage, and tablet_percentage values should typically sum to 100% when representing complete device usage distribution, though individual reports may focus on specific segments.

mobile_percentage.description:
Percentage of platform usage originating from mobile devices.

This metric tracks the proportion of customer interactions, sessions, and transactions conducted through smartphones and other mobile devices. Mobile usage patterns often differ significantly from desktop usage, with higher engagement during evenings and weekends, and different purchasing behaviors.

Understanding mobile percentage helps optimize mobile-first design strategies and prioritize mobile-specific features like touch interfaces, mobile payment integrations, and location-based services.

desktop_percentage.description:
Percentage of platform usage originating from desktop computers.

Desktop usage typically represents customers engaging in more complex shopping activities, such as detailed product research, comparison shopping, and larger purchases. Desktop sessions often have higher conversion rates and larger average order values compared to mobile.

This metric helps understand when customers prefer the full-featured desktop experience versus mobile convenience, informing design decisions for different device contexts.

tablet_percentage.description:
Percentage of platform usage originating from tablet devices.

Tablet usage represents a hybrid experience combining mobile convenience with desktop-like screen real estate. Tablet users often engage in browsing-intensive activities like product discovery, wishlist management, and content consumption.

Understanding tablet usage patterns helps optimize touch interfaces for larger screens and informs decisions about tablet-specific features like split-screen layouts and enhanced media presentation.

mobile_app_vs_browser.description:
Detailed breakdown between mobile app usage versus mobile browser usage.

This reference provides granular analysis of how customers access the platform through mobile devices, distinguishing between dedicated mobile applications and mobile web browsers. The split reveals important insights about customer engagement levels, feature adoption, and platform preferences.

App usage typically indicates higher customer loyalty and engagement, while browser usage represents broader accessibility and lower-friction access patterns.

ICohortRetention.description:
Retention analysis for specific customer acquisition cohorts.

This schema analyzes customer retention patterns for groups of customers acquired during specific time periods (cohorts). Cohort analysis helps understand how retention changes over time and across different customer groups, providing insights into the long-term value of acquisition strategies.

The analysis tracks customer behavior from initial acquisition through subsequent periods, identifying patterns in customer loyalty, churn rates, and lifetime value. This information is crucial for optimizing customer acquisition costs, improving retention strategies, and forecasting long-term business performance.

Cohort retention analysis enables businesses to identify which acquisition channels and customer segments deliver the most sustainable growth, helping prioritize marketing investments and customer experience improvements.

cohort_period.description:
Specific time period when the customer cohort was initially acquired.

This field identifies the acquisition timeframe for the customer group being analyzed, typically formatted as monthly or quarterly periods (e.g., '2024-Q1', 'March-2024'). The cohort period serves as the baseline for tracking retention patterns over time.

Understanding acquisition timing helps correlate retention performance with specific marketing campaigns, seasonal factors, and market conditions that influenced customer acquisition during that period.

initial_cohort_size.description:
Total number of customers in the original acquisition cohort.

This metric represents the baseline customer count acquired during the specified cohort period. The initial cohort size provides context for interpreting retention rates and understanding the scale of customer acquisition efforts.

Tracking cohort size alongside retention patterns helps evaluate the effectiveness of acquisition strategies and provides insights into the relationship between acquisition volume and long-term customer value.

retention_rates.description:
Series of retention rate measurements at different time intervals after customer acquisition.

This array tracks how customer retention evolves over time, typically measuring retention at standard intervals such as 30 days, 90 days, 180 days, and 1 year after acquisition. Each measurement provides insights into customer loyalty at different stages of the customer lifecycle.

The retention rate progression reveals critical patterns in customer behavior, including early-stage churn, mid-term engagement levels, and long-term loyalty. This data helps identify optimal timing for retention interventions and loyalty program enhancements.

IChurnRateAnalysis.description:
Comprehensive analysis of customer churn patterns and contributing factors across the shopping mall platform.

This schema provides detailed insights into customer attrition, including quantitative churn rates, segment-specific patterns, and underlying factors influencing customer departure. Churn analysis serves as a critical business intelligence tool for identifying retention opportunities and optimizing customer lifecycle management strategies.

The analysis encompasses multiple dimensions including overall platform churn rates, breakdowns by customer segments, primary reasons for churn, and predictive indicators that enable proactive intervention. This data supports strategic decision-making for customer retention programs, marketing optimization, and service improvements.

Used primarily in analytics dashboards and reporting systems to monitor customer health and identify at-risk segments before they churn. The schema supports both historical analysis and predictive modeling for customer retention initiatives.

overall_churn_rate.description:
Aggregate customer churn rate expressed as a percentage across the entire shopping mall platform.

Represents the proportion of customers who have stopped using the platform within a defined period. This metric provides a high-level view of customer retention effectiveness and serves as a key performance indicator for customer success initiatives.

Calculated as the number of churned customers divided by the total active customer base, multiplied by 100. Values range from 0 to 100, where higher values indicate greater customer attrition requiring intervention.

churn_by_segment.description:
Detailed churn analysis broken down by specific customer segments and demographics.

Provides granular insights into which customer groups are experiencing higher attrition rates, enabling targeted retention strategies. Segments may include factors like purchase frequency, average order value, geographic location, or product category preferences.

Each segment analysis includes the segment characteristics, churn rate specific to that group, and contributing factors unique to the segment's behavior patterns.

primary_churn_reasons.description:
Identified primary reasons and contributing factors leading to customer churn.

Documents the most common causes of customer departure based on exit surveys, support interactions, and behavioral analysis. Reasons may include service dissatisfaction, competitive offerings, pricing concerns, or user experience issues.

This information helps prioritize improvement initiatives and develop targeted interventions to address the root causes of customer attrition.

churn_prediction_indicators.description:
Predictive indicators and behavioral patterns that signal potential customer churn risk.

Identifies early warning signs and behavioral markers that precede customer departure, enabling proactive retention efforts. Indicators may include declining engagement, reduced purchase frequency, support ticket patterns, or changes in browsing behavior.

Each indicator includes specific metrics, risk thresholds, and predictive strength assessments to prioritize intervention strategies effectively.

IAppBrowserSplit.description:
Comprehensive analysis of mobile platform usage distribution between dedicated applications and mobile browsers.

This schema provides detailed insights into customer preferences for accessing the shopping mall platform through different mobile channels. Understanding the app vs browser split helps optimize development priorities, marketing strategies, and user experience investments.

The analysis examines usage patterns, engagement levels, and conversion rates across mobile platforms to identify opportunities for platform-specific optimizations. This data informs decisions about app feature development, browser optimization, and cross-platform consistency.

Used primarily by product management, marketing teams, and development leads to allocate resources effectively and maximize customer engagement across all mobile access points.

mobile_app_percentage.description:
Percentage of mobile platform usage occurring through dedicated mobile applications.

Represents the proportion of mobile sessions, transactions, or active users accessing the platform via native iOS or Android applications. Higher percentages indicate stronger app adoption and potential for app-specific feature development.

Calculated as app-based mobile usage divided by total mobile usage, expressed as a percentage. Values range from 0 to 100, with industry benchmarks typically showing 60-80% for mature e-commerce platforms.

mobile_browser_percentage.description:
Percentage of mobile platform usage occurring through mobile web browsers.

Represents the proportion of mobile sessions, transactions, or active users accessing the platform via mobile-optimized websites through browsers like Safari, Chrome, or Edge. This metric helps identify opportunities for browser-specific optimizations.

Calculated as browser-based mobile usage divided by total mobile usage, expressed as a percentage. Values range from 0 to 100, complementing the mobile app percentage to total 100% when combined.

app_user_engagement.description:
Comparative engagement level of mobile app users versus browser users on a standardized scale.

Measures the relative engagement intensity across platforms using metrics like session duration, feature usage, conversion rates, or repeat visit frequency. Higher values indicate stronger engagement through the app channel.

Scaled from 0 to 10, where 0 represents minimal engagement difference and 10 indicates significantly higher engagement through apps. Values above 5 typically justify increased investment in app-specific features and optimizations.

IProductCombination.description:
Frequently purchased combination of products identified through basket analysis.

This schema represents a specific combination of products that are frequently purchased together by customers, identified through advanced analytics of shopping basket patterns. Product combination analysis supports bundle recommendations, strategic product placement, and cross-selling opportunities.

Each combination includes the products involved, frequency of occurrence, and confidence level for the combination pattern. These combinations are used for personalized recommendations, promotional bundling, and inventory optimization strategies.

The system tracks combination patterns across different customer segments and time periods to identify emerging trends and seasonal purchasing behaviors. High-confidence combinations are prioritized for marketing campaigns and strategic product positioning.

Used in analytics reports, recommendation engines, and promotional planning systems to enhance customer shopping experiences and increase average order values through targeted product bundling strategies.

combination_id.description:
Unique identifier for the product combination record.

Automatically generated UUID that uniquely identifies this specific combination pattern in the system. Used for tracking combination performance over time and linking combination data across different analytics reports.

The identifier ensures data integrity when referencing specific combinations in recommendation systems and promotional campaigns.

product_list.description:
List of product identifiers that form this frequently purchased combination.

Contains UUIDs of products that are consistently purchased together by customers. The order of products in the list may indicate purchasing sequence patterns or product affinity relationships.

Each product ID must reference an existing product in the shopping mall catalog. The combination analysis validates that all referenced products are active and available for purchase.

Used by recommendation engines to suggest complementary products and by marketing systems to create targeted bundle promotions based on proven purchasing patterns.

frequency_count.description:
Number of times this specific product combination was observed in customer purchases.

Represents the absolute frequency count of how many times customers purchased this exact combination of products together. Higher frequency counts indicate stronger purchasing patterns and more reliable combination recommendations.

The count is accumulated across all customer segments and time periods, providing a comprehensive view of combination popularity. Used to prioritize combinations for marketing and determine statistical significance.

Frequency counts are periodically recalculated to reflect changing purchasing patterns and ensure recommendation accuracy based on current customer behavior trends.

confidence_level.description:
Statistical confidence level indicating the reliability of this product combination pattern.

Represents the probability that this combination pattern is not due to random chance, calculated using statistical methods like association rule mining. Values closer to 1.0 indicate highly reliable patterns with strong predictive power.

The confidence level considers factors like support, lift, and conviction metrics from market basket analysis. High-confidence combinations are prioritized for recommendation systems and promotional campaigns.

Used by analytics systems to filter out spurious correlations and focus on combinations with genuine predictive value for customer purchasing behavior.

IBasketSizeCategory.description:
Category-based analysis of shopping basket sizes and patterns for strategic business insights.

This schema provides comprehensive analysis of shopping basket sizes within specific product categories or customer segments, offering valuable insights into purchasing behavior patterns for different types of products and customer demographics.

The analysis helps understand how basket sizes vary across different categories, supporting inventory planning, category management strategies, and targeted marketing campaigns. By analyzing basket composition and value patterns, businesses can optimize product placement and promotional strategies.

Category-based basket analysis considers factors such as product type, customer preferences, seasonal variations, and pricing strategies to provide actionable insights for improving customer shopping experiences and increasing basket values.

Used in merchandising decisions, inventory optimization, pricing strategies, and customer segmentation to enhance overall shopping mall performance and customer satisfaction through data-driven category management approaches.

category_id.description:
Unique identifier for the category analysis record.

Automatically generated UUID that uniquely identifies this specific basket size analysis for a particular category or customer segment. Used for tracking analysis results over time and comparing performance across different categories.

The identifier ensures data integrity when referencing specific category analyses in reporting systems and strategic planning tools, supporting longitudinal analysis of category performance trends.

category_name.description:
Name of the product category or customer segment being analyzed.

Specifies the specific category (e.g., 'Electronics', 'Home & Garden', 'Fashion') or customer segment (e.g., 'Frequent Shoppers', 'New Customers', 'Premium Members') for which basket size analysis is performed.

The category name provides context for interpreting the analysis results and helps business stakeholders understand which product areas or customer groups the insights apply to. Used for reporting and strategic decision-making.

Category names follow the standardized categorization system used throughout the shopping mall platform, ensuring consistency across different analytical reports and business intelligence tools.

average_items.description:
Average number of items typically found in shopping baskets for this specific category or segment.

Calculated as the mean number of products purchased together by customers within this category. This metric helps understand typical purchasing volumes and supports inventory planning and shelf space allocation decisions.

Higher average item counts may indicate categories where customers tend to make multiple purchases simultaneously, suggesting opportunities for bundle promotions or complementary product placement strategies.

The average is calculated over a significant sample size to ensure statistical reliability and account for seasonal variations and promotional impacts on purchasing behavior patterns.

average_value.description:
Average monetary value of shopping baskets within this specific category or customer segment.

Represents the mean transaction value for purchases involving products from this category, providing insights into customer spending patterns and category profitability. Used for revenue forecasting and pricing strategy optimization.

Higher average values may indicate premium product categories or customer segments with greater purchasing power, while lower values might suggest budget-conscious shopping or impulse purchase categories.

The metric considers both the quantity and pricing of products purchased, offering a comprehensive view of category performance from both volume and value perspectives for strategic business planning.

basket_size_distribution.description:
Detailed distribution analysis of basket sizes within the specified category or segment.

Provides a comprehensive breakdown of how basket sizes are distributed across different value ranges and item counts, offering granular insights into purchasing behavior patterns beyond simple averages.

The distribution analysis helps identify common basket size patterns, outliers, and opportunities for optimization. For example, it might reveal that most baskets fall into a specific size range, suggesting targeted marketing opportunities.

Used by category managers and merchandising teams to understand customer purchasing habits, optimize product assortments, and develop targeted strategies to increase basket sizes through complementary product placement and promotional incentives.

IRetentionRatePeriod.description:
Retention rate at a specific time interval after customer acquisition.

This schema represents the customer retention rate at a particular time period after customers were initially acquired. Period-based retention analysis helps understand how customer loyalty evolves over time and identifies critical retention periods where interventions are most effective.

The analysis provides insights into customer lifecycle patterns and helps optimize timing for retention interventions, loyalty program enhancements, and customer engagement strategies. Retention rates are calculated as the percentage of customers who remain active at each specified period after their initial acquisition.

Used primarily in customer analytics dashboards and retention reporting to track cohort performance over time and measure the effectiveness of customer retention initiatives.

period_after_acquisition.description:
Time period after customer acquisition expressed in standardized format (e.g., '30 days', '90 days', '1 year', '2 years').

This field specifies the exact time interval being measured for retention analysis. Standardized period formats ensure consistency across different analytics reports and enable comparative analysis between different customer cohorts.

Examples include: '7 days' for weekly retention, '30 days' for monthly retention, '90 days' for quarterly retention, and '365 days' for annual retention analysis.

retention_rate.description:
Retention rate percentage at this specific period, calculated as the proportion of customers remaining active.

Expressed as a percentage value between 0 and 100, representing the fraction of the original customer cohort that remains active at the specified period. A retention rate of 75% indicates that 75% of customers acquired during the initial period are still active customers.

This metric is crucial for understanding customer loyalty patterns and identifying optimal intervention points for retention strategies. Higher retention rates indicate better customer satisfaction and product-market fit.

cohort_size.description:
Number of customers remaining in the cohort at this specific period after acquisition.

Represents the actual count of customers who have remained active through the specified period. This absolute number provides context for the retention rate percentage and helps assess the statistical significance of the retention analysis.

Larger cohort sizes provide more reliable retention metrics, while smaller cohort sizes may indicate the need for longer observation periods or combined cohort analysis for statistical validity.

IChurnBySegment.description:
Churn rate analysis for a specific customer segment.

This schema provides detailed churn analysis for a particular customer segment, helping identify which segments are most at risk and why. Segment-based churn analysis enables targeted retention strategies by understanding the unique characteristics and behaviors of different customer groups.

The analysis includes segment-specific churn rates, cohort sizes, and primary contributing factors. This granular approach allows for more effective customer retention interventions by addressing segment-specific pain points and optimizing resource allocation for retention efforts.

Used in customer segmentation analytics, churn prediction models, and targeted retention campaign planning to reduce overall customer attrition and improve lifetime value.

segment_name.description:
Name or identifier of the customer segment being analyzed for churn patterns.

This field identifies the specific customer segment category, such as 'high-value customers', 'new customers', 'geographic region', 'product category users', or other segmentation criteria.

Clear segment naming enables effective communication of churn analysis results and facilitates targeted retention strategies. Examples include: 'premium subscribers', 'enterprise customers', 'North America region', or 'mobile app users'.

segment_churn_rate.description:
Churn rate percentage for this specific customer segment, calculated as the proportion of customers who have discontinued service.

Expressed as a percentage value between 0 and 100, representing the fraction of customers within the segment who have churned during the analysis period. A churn rate of 15% indicates that 15% of customers in this segment have stopped using the service.

This segment-specific churn rate helps identify high-risk customer groups and prioritize retention efforts based on actual churn patterns and business impact.

segment_size.description:
Total number of customers in this specific segment during the analysis period.

Represents the size of the customer segment being analyzed, providing context for the churn rate percentage. Larger segment sizes generally provide more statistically significant churn analysis results.

This metric helps assess the business impact of churn within the segment and guides resource allocation for retention initiatives based on segment importance and size.

primary_churn_factors.description:
Primary factors identified as contributing to churn within this specific customer segment.

This array contains the key reasons or patterns identified as driving churn within the segment. Common factors include: 'price sensitivity', 'product complexity', 'competitor offerings', 'customer service issues', 'feature limitations', or 'usage patterns'.

Understanding these factors enables targeted interventions, such as product improvements, pricing adjustments, or enhanced customer support, specifically designed to address the unique churn drivers within each segment.

IChurnIndicator.description:
Key indicator that predicts potential customer churn based on behavioral, demographic, engagement, or purchase patterns.

Churn indicators are statistical models that identify customers at risk of leaving the platform based on specific metrics and thresholds. These indicators enable proactive retention efforts by flagging customers who exhibit behaviors correlated with churn.

Each indicator includes the specific metric type, threshold values that signal risk, and the predictive strength calculated through statistical analysis. Indicators are used in customer analytics dashboards and automated retention workflows.

The schema supports multiple metric types including behavioral patterns, demographic characteristics, engagement levels, and purchase history to provide comprehensive churn prediction capabilities.

indicator_name.description:
Unique name identifying the churn prediction indicator for reference and tracking purposes. Must be descriptive enough to convey the specific metric being measured, such as 'login_frequency_decline' or 'purchase_value_drop'.

Used in analytics dashboards and reporting systems to identify which specific indicators are triggering churn alerts.

oneOf.description: Behavioral metric tracking customer actions and usage patterns over time, such as login frequency, session duration, or feature usage trends.
Demographic metric based on customer characteristics like age, location, or account tenure that correlate with churn probability.
Engagement metric measuring customer interaction levels with platform features, notifications, or community activities.
Purchase metric analyzing transaction patterns, order frequency, basket size, or spending trends that indicate churn risk.

metric_type.description:
Categorical classification of the metric type used for churn prediction, determining how the indicator data is collected and analyzed.

Each metric type requires different data sources and analysis methods, with behavioral metrics focusing on usage patterns and demographic metrics leveraging customer profile information.

risk_threshold.description:
Numerical threshold value that indicates elevated churn risk when exceeded or unmet, depending on the indicator direction.

For example, a login frequency indicator might trigger at less than 2 logins per week, while a purchase value indicator might trigger at spending below $50 per month.

Threshold values are calibrated through historical data analysis to balance detection sensitivity with false positive rates.

predictive_strength.description:
Statistical measure indicating how strongly this indicator correlates with actual churn events, typically expressed as a value between 0 and 1.

Values closer to 1 indicate stronger predictive power, while values near 0 suggest weak correlation. This metric helps prioritize which indicators to focus on for retention efforts.

Calculated through regression analysis or machine learning models using historical customer data.

ISizeDistribution.description:
Comprehensive distribution analysis of shopping basket sizes across different customer segments, product categories, or time periods.

This schema provides detailed statistical breakdowns of how basket sizes are distributed within the shopping platform, showing patterns in customer purchasing behavior. Distribution analysis helps merchants understand typical purchase volumes and identify opportunities for basket size optimization.

The analysis supports strategic decisions including inventory planning, pricing strategies, promotional targeting, and customer segmentation based on purchasing patterns. Retailers can identify whether their customer base tends toward small frequent purchases or larger consolidated orders.

Size distribution data is essential for optimizing shipping strategies, warehouse management, and product bundling opportunities to increase average order value and customer satisfaction.

size_range.description:
Categorical classification of basket size ranges for segmentation and analysis purposes, such as 'small' (1-3 items), 'medium' (4-7 items), or 'large' (8+ items).

Size ranges are configurable based on business requirements and can be adjusted to match specific product categories or customer segments. The categorization enables simplified reporting and trend analysis across different basket size groups.

item_count_range.description:
Numerical range specifying the minimum and maximum number of items included in baskets within this size category.

Provides precise boundaries for basket size classification, enabling accurate filtering and segmentation. For example, a 'medium' basket might be defined as containing 4 to 7 items inclusive.

The range boundaries are used in analytics calculations to determine which baskets fall into each size category for distribution percentage calculations.

value_range.description:
Monetary value range representing the total spending amount for baskets within this size category, typically in the platform's base currency.

Helps correlate basket size with customer spending patterns, revealing whether larger baskets correspond to higher total values or if customers are purchasing lower-priced items in quantity.

Value ranges are essential for financial analysis, revenue forecasting, and understanding the relationship between basket composition and total order value.

percentage_of_baskets.description:
Percentage value indicating what proportion of total baskets fall into this specific size category during the analyzed period.

Calculated as (number of baskets in category / total baskets) × 100%. This metric helps merchants understand the distribution of basket sizes across their customer base.

High percentages in smaller basket categories may indicate opportunity for cross-selling, while concentration in larger baskets suggests successful bundling strategies.

IShoppingMallDashboardOverview.description:
Comprehensive dashboard overview statistics for the shopping mall platform.

This schema represents aggregated business metrics and system statistics for administrative oversight and business intelligence. It includes key performance indicators across sales, customer engagement, product inventory, and platform activity, providing administrators with a holistic view of platform performance.

The overview aggregates data from multiple Prisma schema tables including shopping_mall_sales, shopping_mall_customers, shopping_mall_products, and shopping_mall_orders. Metrics include total sales revenue, customer growth trends, product inventory status, and order processing statistics. This dashboard data is generated in real-time through aggregation queries without storing pre-computed values, ensuring data freshness and accuracy for administrative decision-making purposes.

Used exclusively in the dashboard overview endpoint for administrative monitoring and business intelligence reporting. The schema provides both high-level summary metrics and detailed breakdowns for deeper analysis of platform performance trends.

totalSales.description:
Total sales revenue generated across all completed transactions in the platform.

Represents the cumulative revenue from all successfully processed sales transactions. This value is calculated by summing the sale_amount field from shopping_mall_sales records where sale_status equals 'completed'. Includes both product sales and any applicable taxes or service fees.

This metric serves as the primary indicator of platform revenue performance and is used for financial reporting, trend analysis, and business growth assessment. The value is updated in real-time as new sales are completed.

totalCustomers.description:
Total number of registered customers in the platform.

Counts all active customer accounts that have completed registration and are eligible to make purchases. This metric is derived from the shopping_mall_customers table, filtering for records where status equals 'active'.

Provides insight into platform adoption and customer base growth. This count excludes suspended, deleted, or inactive customer accounts to ensure accurate representation of the active user base.

totalProducts.description:
Total number of active products available for sale.

Represents the current inventory of products that customers can purchase. This count includes all products from shopping_mall_products where status equals 'active', excluding discontinued, out-of-stock, or temporarily unavailable items.

This metric helps administrators monitor product catalog size and inventory management effectiveness. It reflects the breadth of shopping options available to customers at any given time.

totalOrders.description:
Total number of orders placed in the system.

Counts all purchase orders created by customers, regardless of their current status. This includes orders in various states such as pending, processing, shipped, completed, or cancelled.

Provides a comprehensive view of customer purchasing activity and order volume. This metric helps track platform transaction volume and customer engagement levels over time.

salesToday.description:
Sales revenue generated today.

Aggregates sale_amount from shopping_mall_sales where sale_date matches the current date and sale_status is 'completed'. This provides a daily performance snapshot for quick assessment of today's business activity.

Used for daily revenue tracking and same-day performance comparison. The calculation excludes sales from previous days and includes only transactions finalized on the current date.

newCustomersToday.description:
Number of new customer registrations today.

Counts customer accounts created today from shopping_mall_customers where created_at date matches the current date. This metric tracks daily customer acquisition and platform growth.

Helps administrators monitor registration trends and marketing effectiveness. Only includes customers who completed the registration process successfully on the current day.

ordersToday.description:
Number of orders placed today.

Counts orders created today from shopping_mall_orders where created_at date matches the current date. This provides insight into daily purchasing activity and customer engagement.

This metric helps track order volume fluctuations and identify peak shopping periods. Includes all orders regardless of their current processing status.

averageOrderValue.description:
Average value of completed orders.

Calculated as totalSales divided by totalOrders, providing the mean transaction value across all customer purchases. This metric helps understand customer spending patterns and pricing effectiveness.

Used for revenue optimization and customer behavior analysis. The calculation includes only completed orders to ensure accurate representation of actual revenue per transaction.

topSellingCategories.description:
Top selling product categories by sales volume.

Provides a ranked list of product categories based on sales performance, helping administrators identify market trends and popular product segments.

Each entry includes detailed sales metrics for individual categories, allowing for targeted analysis of category performance and revenue contribution.

recentSales.description:
Most recent sales transactions for quick review.

Displays the latest completed sales transactions with essential details including customer information, product details, and transaction amounts.

Enables administrators to monitor recent platform activity, verify transaction processing, and identify any unusual patterns or trends in real-time.

platformMetrics.description:
Additional platform-level metrics and statistics.

Contains supplementary performance indicators that provide deeper insights into platform health, user engagement, and operational efficiency.

Includes conversion rates, customer retention metrics, inventory turnover, and other business intelligence indicators that support comprehensive platform assessment.

ICategorySalesSummary.description:
Sales summary for a specific product category.

Provides aggregated sales data for individual product categories, showing performance metrics and revenue contribution. This helps administrators identify top-performing categories and market trends for strategic business decisions.

Each summary includes comprehensive metrics including category identification, total sales revenue, transaction volume, and average sale value. This data is essential for category performance analysis, inventory planning, and marketing strategy development.

The schema supports comparative analysis across different product categories, enabling administrators to allocate resources effectively and optimize product assortment based on actual sales performance and customer demand patterns.

categoryId.description:
Unique identifier of the product category from shopping_mall_categories.

References the specific category record in the database, ensuring accurate tracking and reporting of category-specific performance metrics.

This identifier is used to link category sales data with category properties and hierarchical relationships within the product catalog structure.

categoryName.description:
Name of the product category for display purposes.

Provides the human-readable category name that appears in user interfaces and reports. This field ensures clear identification of the category being analyzed.

The category name is sourced from the shopping_mall_categories table and reflects the organizational structure of the product catalog.

totalSales.description:
Total sales revenue generated from products in this category.

Represents the cumulative revenue attributed to this specific product category. Calculated by summing sale_amount values from shopping_mall_sales where the sold products belong to this category.

This metric is crucial for understanding category revenue contribution and identifying high-performing product segments within the overall product assortment.

transactionCount.description:
Number of sales transactions involving products from this category.

Counts the total number of completed sales transactions that include at least one product from this category. This provides insight into category popularity and customer purchase frequency.

Helps administrators understand category engagement levels and identify categories with high transaction volume but potentially lower average transaction values.

averageSaleValue.description:
Average value of sales transactions for this category.

Calculated as totalSales divided by transactionCount, providing the mean transaction value specifically for this product category. This metric helps assess category pricing strategy and customer spending patterns.

Used for category performance benchmarking and pricing optimization. Categories with higher average sale values may indicate premium positioning or successful upselling strategies.

IRecentSale.description:
Recent sales transaction details for dashboard display and business intelligence reporting.

Provides comprehensive information about recent sales transactions including customer details, product information, financial metrics, and transaction timing. This allows administrators to monitor recent platform activity, identify sales trends, and make data-driven business decisions.

Each recent sale includes complete transaction details from the shopping_mall_sales table, linking customer identification, product information, sale amounts, commission calculations, and transaction timestamps. These records are essential for real-time business monitoring and performance analysis.

The schema represents finalized sales transactions that have been successfully processed and paid, providing accurate financial data for reporting and analytics purposes. Recent sales data helps identify popular products, customer purchasing patterns, and platform revenue performance.

Used primarily for administrative dashboard displays, sales reporting, and business intelligence applications where quick access to recent transaction data is required for operational decision-making.

saleId.description:
Unique identifier of the sale transaction from shopping_mall_sales table.

This UUID serves as the primary key for identifying individual sales records and provides a unique reference for tracking transaction history, customer service inquiries, and financial reconciliation processes.

The sale ID links directly to the original order that generated this sale, enabling comprehensive transaction tracing and audit trail maintenance for compliance and reporting requirements.

customerName.description:
Full name of the customer who made the purchase, combining first and last name from customer records.

Provides personal identification for customer service and relationship management purposes while maintaining data privacy by not exposing sensitive customer information like email addresses or phone numbers.

The customer name helps administrators quickly identify purchasing patterns and provides context for customer support interactions when reviewing recent sales activity.

productName.description:
Name of the product sold in this transaction as displayed in the product catalog.

Represents the specific item purchased by the customer, providing context for sales analysis, inventory management, and product performance tracking across the platform.

Product names help identify popular items, seasonal trends, and customer preferences, supporting merchandising decisions and inventory planning based on actual sales data.

saleAmount.description:
Total sale amount including taxes, shipping costs, and any applicable fees.

Represents the gross revenue generated from this transaction before platform commissions and seller payouts. This amount reflects the total customer payment for the purchase.

The sale amount is essential for revenue tracking, financial reporting, and calculating platform performance metrics such as average order value and total sales volume.

saleDate.description:
Timestamp when the sale was finalized and recorded in the system.

Indicates the exact date and time the transaction was completed, providing chronological context for sales analysis, trend identification, and performance reporting over specific time periods.

Sale dates enable time-based analysis of sales patterns, seasonal trends, and platform performance metrics, supporting data-driven business decisions and strategic planning.

itemCount.description:
Total number of items sold in this transaction, representing the quantity purchased.

Indicates the volume of products included in the sale, which helps analyze customer purchasing behavior, basket sizes, and product popularity across different transaction types.

Item count data supports inventory management, shipping cost calculations, and customer behavior analysis by providing insights into typical order sizes and product bundling patterns.

saleStatus.description:
Current status of the sale transaction: completed, refunded, disputed, or other status values.

Provides real-time visibility into transaction state, enabling administrators to monitor sales health, identify issues requiring attention, and track resolution progress for problematic transactions.

Status tracking ensures accurate financial reporting and helps maintain platform integrity by identifying and addressing transaction anomalies or customer disputes promptly.

commissionRate.description:
Platform commission percentage applied to this sale for revenue sharing.

Represents the platform's fee structure for facilitating the transaction, calculated as a percentage of the sale amount. This rate determines the platform's revenue share from each transaction.

Commission rates support financial planning, partner relationship management, and platform sustainability by ensuring appropriate revenue distribution between the platform and sellers.

netAmount.description:
Final amount after commission and fees for seller payout, representing the seller's net revenue.

Calculated as the sale amount minus platform commissions and any applicable transaction fees. This amount represents what the seller actually receives from the transaction.

Net amount tracking ensures accurate financial settlements, supports seller trust and satisfaction, and provides transparency in the revenue sharing model between platform and merchants.

IPlatformMetrics.description:
Comprehensive platform-level metrics and statistics for business intelligence and performance monitoring.

Provides detailed insights into platform performance, user engagement, financial health, and operational efficiency through a comprehensive set of calculated metrics. These indicators support data-driven decision making and strategic planning for platform growth and optimization.

Includes conversion rates, customer retention metrics, inventory turnover, response times, and other key performance indicators that collectively paint a complete picture of platform health and user satisfaction. Each metric is calculated using real-time data from platform operations.

These metrics enable administrators to identify trends, monitor platform stability, optimize user experience, and make informed decisions about feature development, marketing strategies, and resource allocation based on actual performance data.

Used for executive dashboards, performance reporting, investor communications, and strategic planning where comprehensive platform intelligence is required for effective business management and growth optimization.

conversionRate.description:
Platform conversion rate calculated as totalOrders divided by totalCustomers, representing the percentage of registered customers who make purchases.

This critical metric measures the platform's effectiveness at converting registered users into paying customers. A higher conversion rate indicates better user experience, effective marketing, and strong product-market fit.

Conversion rate analysis helps identify opportunities for improvement in user onboarding, product discovery, checkout processes, and overall platform usability that can drive increased revenue generation.

customerRetentionRate.description:
Percentage of customers who have made multiple purchases, indicating customer loyalty and platform stickiness.

Measures the platform's ability to retain customers and encourage repeat business, which is essential for sustainable growth and reduced customer acquisition costs. Higher retention rates indicate strong customer satisfaction and platform value.

Retention analysis supports customer lifecycle management, loyalty program effectiveness, and helps identify factors that contribute to long-term customer relationships and recurring revenue streams.

inventoryTurnover.description:
Inventory turnover rate indicating how quickly products are selling relative to available stock levels.

Calculated as the ratio of cost of goods sold to average inventory, this metric helps optimize inventory management, reduce carrying costs, and improve cash flow by ensuring products move efficiently through the sales pipeline.

Inventory turnover analysis supports purchasing decisions, identifies slow-moving products, and helps maintain optimal stock levels to meet customer demand while minimizing excess inventory and associated costs.

averageResponseTime.description:
Average response time for customer inquiries and support requests measured in seconds or minutes.

Indicates the platform's responsiveness to customer needs and support efficiency. Faster response times correlate with higher customer satisfaction and better issue resolution outcomes.

Response time monitoring helps optimize support operations, identify bottlenecks in customer service processes, and ensure timely assistance for users experiencing issues with the platform.

totalOrders.description:
Total number of orders processed through the platform during the reporting period.

Provides a fundamental measure of platform transaction volume and business activity. Tracking order counts helps monitor growth trends, seasonal patterns, and overall platform usage intensity.

Order volume analysis supports capacity planning, resource allocation, and helps identify periods of high demand that may require additional operational support or infrastructure scaling.

totalCustomers.description:
Total number of registered customers with active accounts on the platform.

Represents the platform's customer base size and market reach. Customer count growth indicates successful user acquisition strategies and platform adoption rates.

Customer base analysis supports marketing effectiveness evaluation, helps forecast revenue potential, and provides context for other metrics like conversion rates and average order values.

activeSellers.description:
Number of sellers actively listing products and processing orders on the platform.

Indicates the health and diversity of the seller ecosystem, which directly impacts product variety, competitive pricing, and overall platform attractiveness to customers.

Active seller tracking helps assess marketplace vitality, supports seller relationship management, and identifies opportunities for seller recruitment and support programs.

averageOrderValue.description:
Average monetary value of orders placed on the platform, calculated as total revenue divided by total orders.

Provides insights into customer spending patterns and transaction economics. Higher average order values indicate stronger customer purchasing power and effective upselling strategies.

AOV analysis supports pricing optimization, product bundling strategies, and helps identify opportunities to increase revenue per transaction through improved merchandising and customer experience enhancements.

IShoppingMallGlobalSearch.IRequest.description:
Global search criteria including search query, filters, and pagination parameters for comprehensive shopping mall platform searches.

This schema defines the request structure for performing comprehensive searches across the entire shopping mall ecosystem. Users can search across products, categories, customers, sellers, sales, orders, coupons, promotions, articles, and reviews with advanced filtering capabilities.

The search request supports text queries with partial matching, entity type filtering, date ranges, price ranges, status filters, and pagination controls to efficiently locate relevant information across the platform. Results are categorized by entity type and include relevant metadata for quick identification of matches.

Security considerations ensure that search results are filtered based on the user's authorization level, with appropriate access controls applied to sensitive customer, seller, and order information. Administrative users have access to comprehensive search results while customer users see filtered results based on their permissions.

The search functionality supports complex queries across multiple entity types simultaneously, with relevance scoring and result ranking based on match quality and entity relationships within the shopping mall platform.

query.description:
Search query text to match against entity names, descriptions, and other searchable fields across the shopping mall platform. Supports partial matching, keyword searching, and fuzzy matching across multiple entity types including products, categories, customers, sellers, and content articles.

Queries can include product names, category titles, customer names, seller business names, article titles, and review content. The search engine performs intelligent matching across all relevant fields with relevance scoring for result ranking.

Maximum query length is 500 characters to ensure optimal search performance across the platform's extensive data set.

oneOf.description: Search across product catalog including product names, descriptions, and attributes
Search across product categories including category names and descriptions
